Consequently, achieving an exact SM prediction for this parameter is essential for effectively searching for new physics. In this study, we calculate $\delta_{\rm CP}$ within the SM with an unprecedented precision of $0.0001$ by incorporating one-loop radiative corrections involving the Higgs boson and top quark. Our findings demonstrate that the precise SM prediction for $\delta_{\rm CP}$ can significantly aid in identifying signatures of new physical phenomena.

The well-mixed model serves as a straightforward framework for describing the spatial distribution of aerosols near an infected person, contrasting with more sophisticated alternatives that incorporate complex turbulent flow patterns. This study evaluates the efficacy of the well-mixed model in predicting local aerosol concentrations by comparing it against both a stochastic Lagrangian framework and a deterministic Eulerian framework. Findings indicate that the well-mixed model performs comparably to these advanced models in generating aerosol concentration forecasts in the immediate vicinity of the source.

The nuclear structure of $^{137}$Te and $^{135}$Te is investigated through $\beta$-decay transitions, utilizing experimental data from the $\beta$-decay of $^{137}$I and $^{135}$I. The study employs the shell model, interacting boson model, and the interacting boson-ferron model to analyze these transitions.

This paper introduces a method for the automatic detection of violations within exchange programs, grounded in recently proven theorems regarding uniqueness. The authors establish a program for synthesizing proof certificates for these exchanges and develop an algorithm to verify said certificates. The approach is demonstrated through multiple examples, with the corresponding source code made available on GitHub.

We predict the masses of $F$-wave bottom mesons by employing a potential model that incorporates both linear confinement and the running strong coupling constant. These predicted masses align well with Regge trajectories and exhibit good agreement with existing experimental data for $S$-wave and $P$-wave bottom mesons.

This paper proves that Szabados's conjecture holds for all minimal periodic decompositions exhibiting low complexity, specifically where the pattern complexity $p(n) \leq 2n+1$. This result extends previous findings by Boshernitzan and others, which established the validity of the conjecture only for $n+1$ pattern complexity.

Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) serves as a powerful technique for extracting coherent structures from data, particularly in nonlinear systems where it has been extended via kernel methods to handle implicit nonlinearities. This study introduces a novel kernelized DMD algorithm that incorporates a linear kernel into the data, offering a more effective approach to nonlinear system analysis. We demonstrate theoretically that this kernelized variant yields superior results compared to the standard DMD method. Furthermore, the paper provides a convergence analysis for the eigenvalues of the resulting Hankel matrix and offers numerical evidence supporting these findings.

This study introduces the application of the Economic Fitness and Complexity (EFC) algorithm to the analysis of chess openings and player competencies. We demonstrate that EFC-derived metrics for chess effectively mirror traditional evaluations, including established opening classifications and player rating disparities. Furthermore, we examine the temporal evolution of these metrics across various dimensions, including specific openings, grandmaster-level games, and historical periods.

We examine the Accretion Induced Collapse (AIC) of white dwarfs within binary systems, a phenomenon that can yield neutron stars. Our analysis demonstrates that the AIC remnant's mass is governed by the white dwarf's initial mass and the quantity of accreted material. We further investigate the evolution of these remnant neutron stars, specifically addressing the accumulation of hydrogen envelopes. Our findings indicate that the subsequent accretion of hydrogen onto these remnants can trigger a second AIC event.

This study presents a novel, direct approach to deriving exact first integrals for higher-order Euler-Lagrange differential equations, specifically applied to the Pais-Uhlenbeck oscillator system. By employing this method, we obtain closed-form expressions for key conserved quantities, including energy, angular momentum, and the Pais-Uhlenbeck integral. Furthermore, we demonstrate that utilizing these first integrals facilitates the integration of the Euler-Lagrange equations, ultimately yielding explicit analytical solutions.

We introduce a new method for retrieving 3D shapes from 3D sketches, a task that is inherently difficult because of the inherent ambiguity in the abstract nature of these designs. To address this, we propose a dual-pathway framework: one branch employs 3D shape retrieval to locate a suitable template, while the other utilizes 3D sketch retrieval to find a similar reference sketch. By integrating results from both pathways, the system effectively narrows the search space and enhances retrieval accuracy. Experiments demonstrate that this dual-path strategy significantly outperforms single-path methods, with sketch-based retrieval yielding superior results for abstract inputs.

We present a detailed analysis of the planet HD 80606 b, a gas giant characterized by an eccentric orbit, utilizing the SPIRou near-infrared spectrograph. This study captures the planet's full trajectory, revealing a substantial variation in effective temperature ranging from 1,000 K to 2,000 K. Our findings indicate that the planet's dayside is dominated by a cool, high-pressure atmosphere, with spectral signatures of water vapor and methane observed in the 1.0–1.1 $\mu$m band, alongside carbon monoxide detected at 2.3 $\mu$m. Furthermore, we have generated the first-ever phase curve for HD 80606 b in the near-infrared spectrum, revealing a peak-to-trough temperature variation of 1,000 K. This extreme fluctuation suggests that atmospheric heat redistribution is minimal, a conclusion supported by our calculated redistribution efficiency factor of $f=1.25$.

We investigate the formation of naked singularities within a spherically symmetric, homogeneous perfect fluid undergoing collapse. Our analysis reveals that while singularities are concealed when the mass profile is uniform, introducing minor irregularities can cause these singularities to become visible. Furthermore, our findings demonstrate that the nature of the resulting naked singularity is highly dependent on the specific characteristics of the perturbed mass profile.

The weak gravity conjecture posits that a consistent quantum gravity framework must include a tower of states whose masses are no greater than the Planck scale. We demonstrate that within a canonical ensemble, satisfying this conjecture necessitates the existence of black holes with minimal mass that can evaporate, resulting in a reduced total mass. Conversely, in a microcanonical ensemble, we show that imposing an upper mass limit on the charged black hole spectrum is equivalent to requiring black hole entropy to be sub-extensive.

Recent research indicates that integrating intrinsic motivation into reinforcement learning (RL) agents can enhance sample efficiency. However, this study demonstrates that merely adding an intrinsic motivation component to an otherwise optimal extrinsic RL policy often degrades performance. We posit that the root cause lies in suboptimal extrinsic learning triggered by the dual reward structure. To address this, we introduce a training framework that simultaneously leverages both intrinsic motivation and extrinsic rewards to boost sample efficiency. Empirical evaluations across various tasks confirm that our proposed method surpasses existing approaches utilizing both reward types in terms of sample efficiency.
This study examines the connection between the coloured Poincaré gravity framework and a specific set of massive and massless particle models.

This paper introduces parameterized algorithms for directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) that are feasible when either the treewidth or pathwidth is used as the parameter. We achieve this by adapting techniques originally developed for directed graphs with bounded directed acyclic width.

This study introduces MemoNav, a novel model designed to enhance navigation efficiency by leveraging a memory mechanism. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to maintain historical context, Memo utilizes a different strategy. It employs a graph-based architecture to represent the environment and incorporates a dedicated mechanism for selectively retrieving relevant information from the graph. This approach allows Memo to bypass the limitations inherent in RNN-based methods. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that Memo achieves significant performance gains, improving navigation efficiency by 15.6% compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

This paper introduces a novel unlicensed spectrum band at 6 GHz, designed for 5G New Radio (NR) and NR-U technologies. We propose a new frame structure optimized for operation in this 6 GHz range and develop a hybrid random access method that combines the strengths of both contention-based and non-contention-based approaches. Simulation results demonstrate that this proposed scheme outperforms existing standard random access protocols, delivering superior system performance.

This study examines the existence of stationary solutions within a system of reaction-diffusion equations featuring both space-dependent influences and diffusive connectivity. We demonstrate that these distinct interaction types drive the formation of spatially heterogeneous patterns. Furthermore, we establish the exponential decay of these solutions at infinity.

We introduce a novel framework for analyzing the evolution of operators within conformal field theories, specifically leveraging the inherent symmetries of the system to streamline calculations of quantities like Hilbert-Schmidt complexity and the averaged out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs). This approach is demonstrated through its application to two-dimensional holographic CFTs, where it yields a more efficient method for computing the OTOCs.

The non-statistical decay of the Hoyle state in $^{12}$C has been investigated using a novel experimental technique involving the simultaneous measurement of $\alpha$-particle energy and time-of-flight. This approach allows for the direct determination of the angular correlation between the Hoyle state's decay products. The findings reveal a two-component structure in the non-statistical decay: a sequential component, which has been identified as the $3^-$ resonance at 7.68 MeV, and a direct component. The study demonstrates that this direct contribution is substantial, accounting for approximately 40% of the non-statistical decay.

This study examines the propagation of brittle cracks influenced by an internal length scale, which becomes significant when material defects are small relative to this dimension. By employing a cohesive zone model, we analyze the problem within a framework of small deformation theory. Our findings indicate that material behavior varies substantially under high loading conditions, a factor that impacts both the trajectory and advancement of cracks. Specifically, we demonstrate that the energy release rate is not solely a function of the crack tip's stress intensity factor but also depends on the internal length scale. Furthermore, we observe that crack paths are not always straight; instead, they can exhibit curvature, a phenomenon that is also modulated by the material's internal dimensions.

We introduce a channel model incorporating causal side information, where the channel's memory capacity is defined by the size of its smallest representation with a finite state. We demonstrate that, for channels with a fixed number of inputs, this memory capacity dictates the channel's capacity. Additionally, we establish a lower bound on the achievable information rate for such channels with a finite state space, a bound that is realized by a specific deterministic channel strategy.

This study examines the interplay between spin-orbit coupling and superconductivity within a two-dimensional electron gas, utilizing the Nambu-spinor formalism to derive the corresponding eigenenergies and eigenstates. We demonstrate that this interaction can transform the system's properties from trivial to topological, with the resulting superconducting phase characterized by an effective mass term that varies dynamically.

This paper details the outcomes of the SEM-TAB-FACTS task, which evaluated natural language generation systems for extracting statements from tables. A total of 10 teams submitted entries across three subtasks, with 10 successful submissions recorded for subtasks 1 and 2, and 8 for subtask 3. The study analyzes the performance of various models and provides an overview of the provided datasets.

This article examines the rationale for employing complex numbers in Quantum Mechanics. It begins by outlining the historical context of complex numbers' usage within the field, followed by a presentation of three distinct arguments supporting their necessity. The paper concludes by addressing frequent objections raised against these viewpoints.

This study examines the impact of graph distance truncation on selecting a metric basis. We demonstrate that for a specific threshold value, the dimension of a graph's metric choice remains unchanged when comparing it to its truncated distance version, provided the original distances exceed this limit. Conversely, for distances below this critical point, the dimension can vary significantly. We further provide an example illustrating that this observed behavior is not merely a coincidence but a general phenomenon.

This study examines the steady-state flow equation for vertical movement of a solute in a porous medium where the horizontal extent is vast. The analysis considers a scenario where hydraulic conductivity changes with vertical position, allowing the flow equation to be reduced to a simplified form. The reduced equation is solved using Laplace transforms, with solutions expressed as inverse transforms. The study further analyzes the solution's behavior in the limit of small diffusion coefficients and compares these findings against the case of constant conductivity.

This study investigates the impact of reactor dimensions and residence time on sulfur dioxide (SO₂) removal efficiency within an O₃-UV system, employing both computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and experimental methods. The CFD model, validated against experimental data, demonstrates strong agreement with measured results. The findings indicate that increasing reactor size or extending residence time enhances SO₂ removal, with the largest reactor achieving the highest efficiency. Furthermore, the study analyzes the effects of inlet ozone concentration and flow rate on SO₂ removal rates. The research concludes that the proposed CFD model effectively predicts the performance of O₃-UV reactors for SO₂ removal.

This paper introduces a comparative analysis of various segmentation architectures employed in large-scale neouromorphic system simulations. We evaluate the performance of four distinct methods: a global approach, per-core segmentation, per-cluster segmentation, and a hybrid model combining per-core segmentation with a global communication layer. The study assesses both the computational speed and the accuracy of the simulated results. Findings indicate that the per-core variant offers the fastest simulation throughput, whereas the global method yields the most accurate outcomes. Furthermore, the proposed per-core-per-cluster hybrid architecture effectively balances simulation fidelity and speed.

Indecision Trees (ITs) are a recently introduced class of models that merge the benefits of probabilistic inference with the efficiency of standard decision trees. While they offer superior performance across various machine learning tasks, their inference process remains slower compared to conventional decision trees. This paper introduces a new pruning strategy designed to accelerate IT inference. Empirical results demonstrate that this approach yields significant speedups, making the model competitive with traditional decision trees in terms of execution time.

Introducing Early Abandoning (EA) has proven to be a highly effective method for enhancing the speed of time series similarity search. Nevertheless, conventional EA approaches often suffer from inefficiency due to the inability to discard non-matching candidates early enough. To address this limitation, we propose a new technique called Quantization-Assisted Early Abandoning (QEA). This approach integrates QEA with the pruning of quantized distance metrics to significantly boost performance. Our evaluation across multiple real-world datasets demonstrates that QEA outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods by a substantial margin.

This study investigates the efficacy of automated feedback mechanisms in programming assignments, specifically examining how different types of information influence student outcomes. We conducted a randomized controlled trial involving 1,000 students across four groups, each receiving distinct levels of guidance: no feedback, code-level feedback, solution-based feedback, or a hybrid approach. Our analysis reveals that while all forms of assistance improve code coverage, only solution-based feedback significantly enhances final grades. Furthermore, we observed that students utilizing higher-quality feedback tended to achieve better grades, indicating that the value of feedback is contingent upon its quality. These findings offer critical insights for educators and practitioners regarding the design and implementation of programming assignment strategies.

Black-box classifiers are frequently employed in high-stakes domains, yet their opaque nature hinders the comprehension of their decision-making processes. While existing methods attempt to address this through local or global model interpretability, symbolic surrogate models offer a robust framework for generating comprehensible approximations of black-box functions. This study introduces a novel approach to refining symbolic surrogates by leveraging domain knowledge to optimize the selection of both the model architecture and its hyperparameters. We validate the efficacy of this method on two distinct datasets: a synthetic data set and the Adult Income data set.

Recent research has highlighted the over-smoothing challenge inherent in Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), a phenomenon that limits their ability to capture fine-grained node details. This study investigates the causes of over-smoothing by examining the theoretical properties of graph filters and the mechanisms of GCNs. We demonstrate that the spectral characteristics of the adjacency matrix and the depth of the network are pivotal factors in this issue. Furthermore, we propose a novel algorithm designed to counteract over-smoothing by explicitly modeling and learning node-specific bias terms. Experimental results across multiple datasets confirm that our method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches.

This study examines simplified frameworks for dark matter particle generation, incorporating both vector and scalar mediators alongside fermionic and scalar dark matter candidates. We evaluate production constraints across various mediator masses and coupling parameters, utilizing data from LHC Run 2 and the XENON1T direct detection experiment.

These functions are derived from the Fourier transform of the light-cone correlator, utilizing a gauge-invariant, non-local operator featuring a bilocal structure with both a longitudinal and a transversely curved Wilson line. We demonstrate that these new functions are intrinsically linked to the light-cone light-ray operator moments, which govern the hadron's light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs). The Compactly Supported Homeomorphism Property (CSHP) is demonstrated for products of the closed long ray (denoted as $L$) and various other topological spaces, including $L$ itself, the ordinal space $\omega_1$, the ordinal space $\omega_1^*$, the sequential fan, the Michael line, and the Sorgenfrey line. Additionally, it is proven that the sequential fan possesses the CSHP.

The epitaxial growth of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) on graphene, which itself rests on a silicon carbide (SiC) substrate, is examined using Raman spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction. The study reveals that the resulting h-BN forms epitaxial relationships with the graphene layer, yielding either a $3^\circ$ or $6^\circ$ rotational alignment relative to the substrate. The prevalence of these specific epitaxial domains is found to depend on the growth temperature. Additionally, the research demonstrates that the Raman spectrum of h-BN exhibits a pronounced sensitivity to its rotational orientation.

This paper introduces a novel estimator for the number of common stochastic trends that remains consistent under both heavy-tailed distributions and large-sample conditions. The method leverages the spectral properties of a specific matrix derived from the sample covariance of detrended time series, where the degree of detrending is determined by the estimated number of trends. The author establishes the consistency of this estimator by analyzing the spectral behavior of the proposed matrix and demonstrating the asymptotic independence of the sample covariance matrices for individual detrended series. Additionally, numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods, particularly when dealing with data exhibiting heavy tails.

We investigate the impact of small-mass perturbers on the weak gravitational lensing distortions produced by galaxy clusters. By utilizing a perturbation framework, we demonstrate that these perturbers induce a modification to the cluster's shear field that is directly proportional to their surface mass density. Our findings indicate that this effect is negligible when the cluster's surface mass density exceeds that of the perturbers by a factor of 100 or more. Furthermore, we show that the covariance between the shear and convergence fields remains unaffected by the presence of these small objects.

This study examines the strategic investment decisions of Internet Service Providers (ISPs) regarding network capacity, considering both cooperative and non-cooperative scenarios. The analysis reveals that cooperation among ISPs leads to higher investment efforts and greater payoffs compared to individual actions, while simultaneously reducing total content provider costs. Furthermore, the paper addresses the challenge of enabling cooperation through the design of incentive-compatible mechanisms.
We demonstrate that the weak naturality condition imposed on 2-cells within 2-categorical frameworks is sufficient to guarantee both the naturality and universal properties of resulting adjunctions.

We evaluate the compatibility of exponential and polynomial $\alpha$-attractor models with current cosmological datasets. Our analysis reveals that exponential attractors provide a superior fit to the data compared to polynomial variants. Furthermore, we examine the implications of these models for inflationary dynamics and the generation of primordial gravitational waves.

We demonstrate that for any Fuchsian manifold, quasi-Fuchsian manifolds in a sufficiently small neighborhood can be uniquely determined by the bending laminations of their conformal structures at infinity, provided these laminations are filling. Additionally, we prove that the space of all such filling bent laminations forms a dense subset within the topological boundary of the quasi-Fuchsian Teichmüller space.

This study examines the moments of cross-sectional return distributions, demonstrating that the first four align with those of a weighted sum of individual asset returns, where weights correspond to each asset's cross-sectional dispersion of returns. The research further analyzes the implications of these findings for asset pricing models and the estimation of risk premiums.

This study introduces a novel approach for detecting cardiac abnormalities by employing a variational autoencoder (VAE) to learn latent representations from noisy single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. The proposed method utilizes a reconstruction error metric to identify anomalies, demonstrating through experiments on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database that it outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques.

We present an electric dipole calculation for the $2p\,^2P_{1/2} \to 1s\, ^2S_{1/2}$ transition in muonic hydrogen, partitioning the result into Main, Core, and Tail components. The Main term, representing the one-loop radiative correction involving the Coulomb potential, is computed using the Mellin-Barnier technique combined with the method of regions. The Core component, arising from the radiative correction's short-distance behavior linked to the potential's non-perturbative nature, is evaluated via a subtraction method. The Tail, accounting for long-distance effects where perturbation theory applies to the smooth potential correction, is determined numerically.
We introduce a novel framework for analyzing twists within finite group actions on a torus, utilizing this approach to calculate equivariant cohomology for such scenarios.

This paper explores the connection between the departmental climate and the sense of community and collaboration within it. Drawing on the literature, we outline strategies for fostering a positive departmental environment, with a specific focus on supporting faculty members.

This study examines the fractional series operator $T_{\alpha}$ acting on the unit circle $\mathbb{T}$. Under the condition $1 < p \leq q < \infty$, we establish that $T_{\alpha}$ is unbounded from $H^{p}(\mathbb{T})$ into $H^{q}(\mathbb{T})$ whenever $\alpha \in (0,1)$, thereby resolving a query originally raised by D. E. Edmunds and J. Langenbruch.

This paper investigates seller behavior in second-price auctions featuring non-credible common-value uncertainty. We demonstrate that, contrary to theoretical expectations, sellers often fail to maximize revenue due to behavioral deviations, specifically rule violations and suboptimal bidding strategies. Our findings indicate that these deviations are driven by a combination of loss aversion, mental accounting, and the influence of reference points.

This study examines the evolution of anisotropic spatial geometries within a universe containing a perfect fluid, utilizing the Einstein field equations. The analysis demonstrates that anisotropy diminishes over time, eventually leading to an isotropic state. Additionally, the paper investigates the feasibility of generating anisotropic cosmological models through the application of anisotropic initial conditions.

We investigate the $G$-orbit closures within the flag variety that correspond to Hessenberg varieties, where $G$ denotes the group of upper-triangular matrices. By utilizing a specific realization of these Hessenberg varieties as zero-level sets of polynomials, we identify the generators of the local defining ideals at each singularity. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these ideals admit Gr\"obner bases.

The emergence of AI art, particularly through GANs, has sparked significant debate regarding the definition of creativity. This paper explores how these models, specifically by generating brushstrokes for paintings, can be utilized to create artworks.

The recent flavor anomalies observed in the $K$ and $B$ meson systems, which challenge lepton-flavor universality, have prompted investigations into the validity of the Standard Model. This study examines the impact of these anomalies on the mixing of $B_s$ and $B_d$ mesons. We analyze the constraints imposed by the measured mixing frequency ratio, $x_s/x_d$, alongside the mixing phase difference, $\phi_s/\phi_d$, derived from the rare decay $B \to J/\psi K^0$. Our findings indicate that the anomalies exert a significant influence on the mixing phase $\phi_s/\phi_d$, whereas their effect on the mixing frequency ratio $x_s/x_d$ remains negligible.

We introduce the **QASPER** dataset, comprising 100,000 diverse natural language questions paired with their corresponding answers. To address the challenges of Question Answering (QA), we developed a new architecture that integrates a question encoder, an answer encoder, and an answer retrieval module. Empirical results demonstrate that our proposed model significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches on the **QASPER** benchmark. Additionally, we released the **QASPER** dataset publicly to support further research and development in the QA field.

We examine the impact of neutrino heating on the stability of the forward shock in core-collapse supernovae. Our findings indicate that while neutrino heating can trigger a fast instability in the post-shock region, this effect is contingent upon the explosion's outcome. Specifically, in successful explosions, the instability is confined to a narrow zone immediately behind the shock front. Conversely, in failed explosions where the shock stalls, the instability extends deeply into the accretion torus. Consequently, the instability's ability to drive an explosion is limited, as it cannot effectively revive the stalled shock.

This study introduces a novel classification framework for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) utilizing modified deep learning architectures. The methodology involves training a ResNet-50 model on the ADHD-200 dataset to identify key Regions of Interest (ROIs) within facial images. Subsequently, these significant ROIs are extracted and fed into two distinct models: a standard Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a ResNet variant. Experimental results indicate that the ResNet model surpasses the conventional CNN, achieving an accuracy of 70.46% while being trained on a reduced set of 100 ROIs selected from the original 1,000. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that model performance remains robust even when training data is limited to just 10% of the available dataset.

This paper establishes the existence and uniqueness of an interior fixed point for a specific class of non-linear operators within a partially ordered Banach space. Furthermore, it demonstrates the convergence of an iterative sequence toward this fixed point. These findings are illustrated by a counterexample and applied to a problem involving the uniqueness of positive solutions in a nonlinear model.

We introduce a system designed to identify and disambiguate acronyms across diverse writing domains. This system is built on a new dataset comprising 1,000 documents, which we have annotated with 100,000 acronym instances.

Heat rectification, or directional control of thermal currents, is a fundamental concept in thermoelectrics. This study demonstrates that quantum Hall systems can achieve heat rectification by utilizing a tunable thermal conductance between edge states. By employing a model based on phonon scattering, we illustrate how to modulate this conductance via the edge states' confinement length. Furthermore, we show that combining this mechanism with an asymmetric potential landscape results in efficient thermal rectification.

This study introduces a novel framework for DNA primer pair design, specifically targeting the mitigation of hybridization between primers to ensure efficient data storage partition management. We present a new algorithm that maps primers to partitions while preventing unintended cross-partition hybridization, a critical factor for partition isolation. The efficacy of this approach is validated through a comparison of its generated partition counts against those produced by the existing dStore system.

We introduce a novel three-dimensional nodal-line semimetal characterized by two parallel nodal lines in momentum space. This state is realized within a hyperhubbard model defined on a 16-site unit cell, which is constructed by combining two 4-site unit cells of the kagome lattice. The system's nodal lines are protected by a combination of mirror symmetry and a quantized mirror Chern number. The 16-site unit cell is generated by stacking four distinct kagome configurations: one standard kagome lattice alongside three variants featuring different sublattice occupation patterns. The research demonstrates that the system's band structure and topological attributes can be tuned by varying the hopping parameters and on-site energies.

This study examines the propagation of oscillation-induced waves within a medium, specifically analyzing the velocity of these waves. The findings indicate that wave speed is determined by the medium's density and elasticity. Furthermore, the research highlights the significance of wave interference and diffraction, demonstrating how these phenomena affect the overall propagation.

This paper introduces a novel, computationally efficient, and unbiased algorithm for estimating entropy that performs optimally when input entropy is bounded away from zero. The study rigorously proves the algorithm's consistency and demonstrates that its variance is optimal up to a constant factor. Furthermore, the paper establishes a lower bound on the variance for any unbiased estimator, demonstrating that the proposed method achieves this bound. Simulation results are provided to validate the theoretical findings.

Imaging biobanks are increasingly pivotal for developing artificial intelligence (AI) tools in biomedical research. However, the planning and execution of these repositories often lack standardized guidelines, resulting in data collections that may be ill-suited for AI. This article outlines best practices for establishing imaging biobanks specifically designed to support AI, with a focus on data management, governance, and quality assurance. We further examine emerging standards and technologies that can enhance the efficacy of these databases.

This study investigates data augmentation techniques for predicting COVID-19 status using electronic health records (EHR) from the MIMIC-III dataset. We evaluate multiple strategies, including random flipping, random masking, and feature mixing, assessing their performance across varying levels of clinical feature availability. Results indicate that feature mixing outperforms other methods, particularly in scenarios with limited clinical data, while also demonstrating that clinical features significantly enhance the efficacy of data augmentation.

We introduce and investigate a family of polymatroidal ideals, parameterized by a specific class of directed graphs. This study examines various algebraic and combinatorial characteristics of these ideals and their associated rings, with particular emphasis on their linear quotients and polymatroidal attributes.

We introduce a quantum algorithm for K-means clustering that operates with an asymptotic complexity of $O(poly(n))$, representing a substantial improvement over the $O(exp(n))$ cost of standard classical approaches. This work presents the first fully quantum implementation of the algorithm, utilizing only quantum subroutines for arithmetic operations and data storage. We validate the approach through simulations on both synthetic and real-world datasets, confirming its efficacy.

We introduce a novel method for identifying planetary transits in Kepler data by leveraging the unique characteristics of post-crossing event (PCE) light curves. This approach successfully detects 1,022 PCEs, including 102 instances where the associated main transits were previously unidentified. By combining these findings with existing Kepler results, we derive a more comprehensive planet mass-ratio function, $f(m_2/m_1)$, which peaks at approximately $0.15$ and extends up to $0.5$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that PCEs offer a valuable resource for discovering planets with long periods and low mass ratios.

This study introduces a novel shadow computation technique that improves upon traditional ray tracing by utilizing a pre-calculated, pre-mapped ray distribution. This method is integrated into a path tracer to generate high-quality images with reduced computational costs. The paper details the design of the shadow map, its implementation within the path tracer framework, and the specific modifications required. Additionally, it presents a new, streamlined approach for determining visibility between surfaces. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves significant performance gains while maintaining visual fidelity.

This study introduces a novel approach to estimating the covariance matrix for probabilistic Origin-Destination (O-D) demand modeling using Lasso regularization. By applying Lasso, the method reduces the covariance matrix's dimensionality, thereby mitigating the challenges associated with high-dimensional estimation. Simulation results demonstrate that this regularization technique significantly enhances estimation accuracy. Furthermore, the study evaluates the performance of the proposed Lasso-based estimator against two existing methods: the traditional inversion of the sample covariance matrix and the Method of Moments.

This study investigates the stability of phase-locked configurations within a ring oscillator featuring weak nonlinear frequency dispersion. By employing a perturbative technique, we derive an expression for the locked state's stability that aligns with findings from numerical simulations.

Uniform spanning trees (USTs) are fundamental objects in probability theory, and algorithms by Jonsson and by Kotecký, peres, and others have been developed to generate them. This paper introduces a hybrid algorithm that combines these two methods, significantly improving efficiency by reducing the number of random bits required to produce a UST. We prove that the hybrid algorithm's runtime is bounded by $O(n^2)$, which is a notable improvement over the original methods. Additionally, we show that the algorithm's output is a valid UST with high probability. Finally, we demonstrate that the algorithm's output is a valid UST with high probability.

We introduce the MusicMD-Dataset, a comprehensive collection of 100,000 MIDI pieces paired with corresponding lyrics, designed to advance representation learning for music through cross-modal retrieval. To achieve this, we developed a transformer-based architecture capable of jointly encoding both audio and textual data. Furthermore, we established a new evaluation metric called CrossModal Retrieval Accuracy (CMRA) to assess the quality of generated latent embeddings. Experimental results demonstrate that our model significantly outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods on the MusicMD-Dataset.

We introduce "Ontodia," a web-based platform designed for the visual exploration of extensive, structured datasets, such as Wikidata. This tool empowers users to construct interactive queries through a user-friendly interface, with results presented as dynamic, multi-view visualizations. Users can refine their searches by incorporating ontology concepts, and the system supports the creation and sharing of personalized dashboards.

This paper investigates the orbital stability of traveling dark solitons within the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation. We demonstrate that for wave speeds $c$ sufficiently close to zero, these solitons are orbitally stable. This finding extends previous research by the second and third authors, which established stability only for symmetric black solitons. Additionally, we provide numerical evidence suggesting orbital instability for all non-zero black soliton types.
This paper introduces the Lotse library, a Python-based tool designed to facilitate the implementation of guidance strategies.

This study investigates the flexibility of nested flux surfaces in a two-coil system, analyzing how coil placement influences achievable configurations. We demonstrate that positioning both coils within the same plane maximizes flexibility, whereas placing them in separate planes significantly restricts it. Furthermore, our findings indicate that a two-coil setup can only sustain a single equilibrium state; this state is defined by a specific rational surface radius determined by the coil parameters. We also quantify the resulting volume of the nested flux surfaces and evaluate the impact of varying the minor radius of the control coils on this flexibility.

This study introduces a novel, cost-effective method for monitoring temperature in reactors by utilizing the proton resonance frequency's temperature-dependent shift. The approach employs a single, conventional radio-frequency coil, eliminating the need for specialized hardware. The paper details the design and construction of a prototype system, followed by an analysis of its performance.

This study examines the formation of distinct condensates in multi-component mixtures, demonstrating that up to $N-1$ separate condensates can emerge from an $N$-species system. We establish that the resulting phase diagram is governed by the interplay between the relative concentrations of the species and their pairwise interaction strengths. Furthermore, we derive the conditions under which the system's free energy is minimized, thereby confirming the thermodynamic stability of this phase-separated state.

Magnetic transients are rapidly evolving, compact features that emerge during solar flares and travel across the Sun's surface at speeds ranging from 100 to 1,000 km/s. These phenomena are hypothesized to be magnetic flux ropes generated by reconnection events within the corona. This study examines the magnetic field structures of these transients as they move through sunspots, utilizing high-resolution data from the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST) and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). Our analysis reveals that these features are compact, with dimensions of approximately 1,000 x 1,000 x 1,000 km, and possess strong, concentrated magnetic fields exceeding 1,000 Gauss. Furthermore, the transients display a distinct hourglass morphology, characterized by a narrow waist and bulbous ends, which aligns with the predictions of the flux rope model.

The Badsen-Weiss theorem is a stability result concerning the $b$-principle for formal $b$-structures on 4-dimensional manifolds. This work extends that theorem to the realm of $b$-manifolds with boundary.

This study examines the Balancing Domain Decomposition by Constraints (BDDC) preconditioner applied to the semi-discrete time formulation of the heat equation. We demonstrate that the BDDC spectrum remains independent of both the temporal step size and the number of subdomains, relying solely on interfacial geometric factors. Additionally, the work extends previous findings by E. Arge et al. regarding the analysis of the BDDC method for time-dependent parabolic problems to include non-uniform time-stepping approaches.

This paper investigates user behavior within tagging systems, specifically focusing on the DigiLib project, a research initiative at the University of Trento dedicated to exploring advanced metadata systems. By analyzing user activity, the authors propose insights that can inform the design of improved tagging mechanisms and new content management features.

This study investigates how thermoviscous effects influence the acoustic response of microscale metamaterials, a factor critical to their design. The paper presents a hybrid framework combining the full linearized Navier-Stokes equations with a simplified adiabatic approximation of the entropy equation. The associated system is solved using a finite element method, with results compared against an acoustics-only model that neglects thermoviscous terms. The analysis focuses on a unit cell featuring a microscale air channel, and the findings demonstrate that these effects substantially modify both the magnitude and phase of the scattering matrix.

This study examines the low-frequency behavior of solutions within the context of the FENE dumbbell model, which represents a specific class of viscoelastic fluids. We establish that, under a low-frequency condition, the solution's decay rate aligns with that of the corresponding Stokes problem when measured in Besov spaces.

This study investigates the optimal placement of mobile Integrated Access and Backhaul (mIAB) base stations (BSs) to enhance service for user equipment (UE) clusters in motion. The research focuses on a scenario where both the locations of the BSs and the trajectory of the UE groups are optimized. The primary goal is to maximize the total data rate for all UE groups, subject to the power limits of the BSs and the capacity of the wireless links. The optimization framework is formulated as a non-convex problem, which is then addressed using an iterative algorithm that alternates between optimizing the BS positions and the movement paths of the UE groups. Simulation results demonstrate that this proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of spectral efficiency.

The stability of algorithm performance is frequently influenced by hyperparameters, which often interact with one another. This study investigates how these interactions affect the stability of the k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN) classifier. We introduce a novel methodology for identifying interacting pairs of hyperparameters and demonstrate its application to the kNN classifier using the Adult dataset. Our findings reveal that the interaction between the k parameter and the distance metric is notably significant. Additionally, we present a new approach for tuning kNN that leverages these interaction insights to achieve enhanced predictive performance.

This work examines the quantization of the electromagnetic field's energy, which is essential for explaining the Balmer series. We demonstrate that the energy of the emitted radiation is proportional to the frequency of the transition, thereby validating the quantization principle.

Curriculum learning involves dynamically adjusting training data difficulty to guide an agent toward optimal performance. While beneficial, its effectiveness hinges on carefully designing these controlled transitions, a challenge that is difficult to evaluate due to the vast space of possible curriculum structures. To address this, we introduce CurRies—a novel framework that treats curriculum design as a meta-learning task. By employing a hierarchical structure, CurRies automatically generates and optimizes specific difficulty schedules. Experimental results across three distinct environments demonstrate that methods trained with CurRies-enhanced curricula consistently outperform those using standard random training or manually constructed curricula.

Liger is a Python-based framework designed for processing large-scale astronomical datasets, featuring a Data Reduction System (DRS) that orchestrates the execution of numerous reduction steps on extensive data collections. This paper details the implementation of a Dler for the Gaia mission, which manages over 100 reduction steps involving more than 100 million stars. We also present the outcomes of a pilot run conducted on a subset of this data.

This study examines the existence of traveling wave solutions near the Couette flow in the context of the 2D Navier-Stokes equations with periodic boundary conditions. By utilizing a specialized weighted $L^2$-based Littlewood-Paley framework, we establish that such waves exist provided the regularity parameter $\sigma$ satisfies $0 < \sigma < 1/2$. This finding notably extends previous research by Chen, Kato, and Pu (2019), who required $\sigma > 1/2$, thereby lowering the necessary smoothness threshold.

We introduce a novel approach to manipulating polarization, which could significantly advance fields like spintronics and nonlinear optics. This method utilizes a single, uncoated, and unpatterned silicon nanowire to transform the polarization state of light.

This study examines the behavior of Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KZP) equations with multiplicative noise and the Laplacian term, specifically focusing on solution existence when the parameter $\lambda$ is small versus large. For sufficiently small values of $\lambda$, we establish the non-existence of solutions, whereas for sufficiently large $\lambda$, we prove existence. These findings are derived from a novel approach to analyzing the regularity of noise, which is applicable to a broader class of stochastic partial differential equations.

This paper examines the difficulties encountered in accessing and interpreting South Africa's publicly available COVID-19 datasets, which are essential for understanding the epidemic's trajectory. The authors analyze the obstacles faced by data scientists and policymakers in extracting actionable insights from these records. The study employs a mixed-methods approach, combining an analysis of the data's technical attributes with semi-structured interviews involving stakeholders. The findings reveal that the datasets are plagued by errors, inconsistencies, and a lack of clarity, rendering them unsuitable for direct analysis. The authors conclude by offering recommendations to improve the quality of government data and suggest pathways for future research.

This paper investigates the characteristics of finite integer subsets where the maximum number of addends in any of their subset sums is limited. We demonstrate that imposing a bound on arithmetic progression lengths significantly alters these set properties. Additionally, we provide an example illustrating that such sets can exhibit exponential growth.

This study introduces Hierarchical Fusion, a novel approach designed to integrate data from multiple modalities. Unlike early fusion, which combines inputs at the outset, or intermediate fusion, which merges them after individual processing, Hierarchical Fusion dynamically weighs the contribution of each source. We validate the method's efficacy through experiments on three distinct tasks: multi-label classification, multi-instance classification, and multi-source object detection.

The COVID-19 pandemic has severely strained healthcare systems worldwide, particularly by overwhelming Intensive Care Units (ICUs). This study introduces a novel approach to ICU resource allocation by analyzing factors that predict admission, specifically targeting the detection of high-risk patients. We developed a classification model utilizing data from the COVID-19 ICU registry in Spain, which includes 1,000 patient records. The model's performance was validated through rigorous testing, demonstrating a balanced accuracy of 0.82, a precision of 0.82, and a recall of 0.82. These findings indicate that the proposed method offers a robust solution for optimizing ICU resource management during the pandemic.

This study examines the localization of transmission eigenfunctions within a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^N$ featuring radially symmetric boundaries and characterized by constant medium parameters $\theta$ and $\beta$. The analysis demonstrates that these eigenfunctions exhibit concentration near the domain's boundary under the conditions of a constant $\theta$ and $\beta$. Furthermore, the paper derives the asymptotic behavior of the corresponding transmission eigenvalues.

Recent advances in speech technology have largely stemmed from pre-training models on massive, unlabeled datasets, with current research predominantly focusing on single-task approaches. In contrast, this study introduces a multi-task pre-training framework designed to enhance utterance representations through diverse speech tasks. We evaluate various multi-task strategies and demonstrate that a weighted ensemble of individual single-task models outperforms alternative methods. Applied to the task of automatic speech recognition (ASR), this proposed approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods.
The functor $W$ on simplicial groups forms a monad, with its unit and multiplication maps corresponding to the inclusion and universal bundle functor, respectively.

This study examines the continuum limit of a discrete model featuring $N$ particles on $\mathbb{Z}$ governed by the fully nonlinear, integrable, and completely integrable Hietarinta-Olver system. By utilizing a specific scaling technique, the variable $S^{(1,0)}$ converges to the continuum described by the integrable Korteweg-de Vries equation. Additionally, the paper establishes the convergence of the joint distribution of the initial positions of the first $k$ particles to the Airy process, with the proof relying on the convergence of the associated $\beta$-ensemble to the $\beta$-Airy process.

Detecting relationships between visual elements is a fundamental yet difficult task in computer vision. Although current methods have largely focused on optimizing proposal generation, they often overlook the critical aspect of optimizing the relationship model itself. To address this imbalance, we introduce Balanced Negative Proposal Sampling (BNPS), a strategy designed to balance positive and negative samples during optimization. BNPS achieves this by selecting negative proposals that are most similar to positive ones, thereby enhancing the discriminative power of the model. Furthermore, we propose a new training framework that jointly optimizes proposal generation and relationship modeling, which synergistically improves overall performance. Extensive experiments on the ROCO and gRel datasets demonstrate that our approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques.

We demonstrate that residual quantumness within a quantum system can be retrieved via weak measurements applied to the probe. Specifically, we show that the quantum attributes of the system are re-established through the reversal of these weak interactions.

We introduce a novel method for modeling the evolution of social connections through a relational graph utilizing Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) to manage the dual tasks of updating relationship attributes and forecasting link formation. By applying GRUs, the system effectively captures both the historical progression of these relationships and the current status of associated nodes. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that this approach surpasses existing methods in accuracy for predicting whether a connection will be established.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) have become essential for addressing challenges across numerous domains, yet their computational complexity often renders them impractical for real-time applications. To mitigate this, we introduce a method for adaptively sampling nodes to create subgraphs, thereby lowering computational demands. Our approach employs a reinforcement learning framework to train a sampling policy that balances inference speed with predictive accuracy. Specifically, we define a reward function that evaluates the quality of each sampled subgraph. Experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate that our technique achieves significant reductions in computational complexity while maintaining high prediction performance.

This paper introduces a novel methodology for designing Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) circuits that incorporates error propagation rules to enhance implementation efficiency. The proposed approach leverages a new class of rational number representations, termed "Rational Chains," which facilitate the integration of bit-level error propagation analysis throughout the MCM design workflow. Simulation results demonstrate that this technique yields superior outcomes compared to state-of-the-art methods.

Recent years have seen significant advancements in deep learning, inspiring numerous investigations into its quantum counterpart. Despite this growing interest, research on quantum deep learning remains in its infancy, primarily due to the absence of a robust theoretical framework. This paper introduces a theoretical model for quantum neural networks (QNNs) designed to address classification challenges. We establish convergence bounds for these networks and demonstrate that QNNs can achieve comparable classification accuracy to classical neural networks with reduced circuit depth. Furthermore, we outline a strategy for mitigating the barren plateau phenomenon within QNNs.

Advancements in radio frequency technology have significantly broadened the scope of accelerator applications beyond high-energy physics, benefiting fields such as free-electron lasers, medical accelerators, and compact accelerators. This paper examines the progress made in RF systems and components, with a specific emphasis on the development of high-impedance slow-wave structures.

The High-Luminosity Muon Collider (ML) stands as a highly anticipated future particle accelerator, yet it faces significant hurdles in design and operation due to the unique properties of muons. This paper reviews the current status of the Muon Collider project, emphasizing the unique challenges posed by the species and outlining the necessary advancements. We examine the status of key R&D efforts, including muon beam dynamics, acceleration techniques, and detector design. Furthermore, we explore the progress made in muon source development and the simulation of experimental data.

This paper investigates the dispersion relations of scalar and vector modes within viscous relativistic fluid frameworks, specifically examining the frameworks proposed by Muller-Israel-Starr (MIS) and Landau-Lifshitz (LL). We demonstrate that the MIS model yields dispersion relations identical to those derived from the Gubser, Fuchs, and Minic (GFM) formulation, whereas the LL model produces distinct results. Furthermore, we establish that the dispersion relations in the GFM model differ from those in the viscous relativistic kinetic theory based on the Boltzmann equation. Finally, we analyze the stability of the GFM model and confirm its stability.

This study examines the gravitational radiation emitted by primordial black holes (PBHs) across a mass spectrum ranging from $10^{15}$ g to $10^{23}$ g. We demonstrate that the peak of the Hawking radiation spectrum shifts toward lower frequencies for more massive PBHs, resulting in a significantly higher flux of low-energy photons compared to previous calculations. Additionally, we analyze the influence of cosmological expansion on the emitted spectrum and find that its impact is negligible. Finally, we explore the consequences of these findings for PBH evaporation scenarios.

This paper introduces a pipelined circuit evaluator that leverages a hardware architecture to accelerate circuit evaluation. The proposed design is implemented within a single-cycle framework, enabling concurrent processing of multiple clock cycles. The work details the design and validation of this architecture, including a comparative analysis against existing methodologies.

This paper demonstrates that a PTAS exists for certain classes of minimization General-Valued CSPs (GVCS) featuring crisp constraints, specifically when the polymorphisms are partially weighted and satisfy a condition equivalent to being weighted majority-closed. Additionally, we establish a new structural characterization of these crisp constraint GVCS instances admitting a PTAS.

This study introduces FPIO, a novel few-shot parsing model designed to handle hierarchical structures. It employs a two-stage framework: first, a pre-training phase utilizes large volumes of unlabeled data to build an initial model, followed by fine-tuning on small sets of annotated trees. Experiments across various hierarchical structure datasets demonstrate that FPIO surpasses existing few-shot parsing approaches, particularly in scenarios requiring only five training trees. Furthermore, the model exhibits robust generalization to unseen hierarchical types.

Recent advancements in deep learning have significantly enhanced the performance of semantic segmentation, particularly in applications like agriculture where detailed labeling is crucial. However, acquiring such detailed labels remains costly and time-consuming. This study investigates whether utilizing less expensive, coarse labels from hyperspectral images can effectively train high-performance segmentation models. We demonstrate that a model trained on coarse data can achieve results comparable to one trained on fine labels by employing an auxiliary loss function designed to maximize the agreement between coarse predictions and fine ground truth. Empirical results confirm that this approach yields competitive segmentation accuracy while drastically reducing annotation expenses.

We report the findings of a multi-epoch, multi-wavelength campaign focused on KIC 9267654, a solar-type star identified by the Kepler mission for its anomalous rotation curve. Our analysis of high-precision photometry from TESS and Kepler, combined with radial velocity measurements from the HARPS spectrograph, reveals a stable 1.021-day rotation period and a stellar mass of 0.91 ± 0.03 M☉. While the star exhibits a typical activity cycle of approximately 1.5 years, characterized by variations in spot coverage and line bisector spans, our data indicate a persistent, long-term trend in the rotation period. This secular change amounts to roughly 1.5 seconds per year, a phenomenon potentially attributable to tidal interactions with a distant companion or magnetic braking effects.

We introduce a RAM model capable of manipulating polynomial integers with $O(1)$ efficiency per coefficient, alongside an extension supporting modular arithmetic over polynomial rings. This framework enables the construction of a RAM model for algebraic integers in any number field, which we leverage to design a new algorithm for polynomial GCD computation. This approach surpasses the efficiency of current methods, which are limited by the bit-complexity constraints of standard RAM models.

Self-supervised learning has emerged as a powerful technique for enhancing representation learning in session-based recommendation by improving data augmentation. This study introduces a self-supervised approach to bolster the session encoding capabilities of Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs). The proposed method leverages the inherent temporal and sequential nature of sessions to create effective data augmentation strategies. Furthermore, it employs a contrastive learning framework to train the augmented data, resulting in superior representation quality. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms both traditional and existing self-supervised baselines.

This paper investigates linear complementary dual (LCD) codes derived from group rings. We demonstrate that constraints imposed on group ring elements can significantly influence the attributes of the generated LCD codes. Additionally, we provide specific instances of binary and ternary linear complementary dual codes derived from these group rings.
This work demonstrates that certain invariant differential forms generate the stable real cohomology of the group's general linear transformations.

This study investigates how auxiliary variables influence the ability of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to learn object categorization. We demonstrate that RNNs equipped with these variables achieve superior object categorization performance compared to standard models. Furthermore, we reveal that the presence of auxiliary variables enhances the interpretability of internal RNN states by aligning them more closely with semantic concepts.

This study examines the skin effect within extended non-Hermitian chains, utilizing the modified Hatano-Nelson model as a primary example. We demonstrate that correlations arising from the lack of biorthogonality between eigenstates and the influence of non-Hermiticity interact to produce a generalized skin effect. Analytically, we derive the relationship linking the magnitude of the spectral skin depth to that of the oscillatory skin depth. Furthermore, we extend our analysis to a broader class of long-range non-Hermitian chains, revealing that correlations can either amplify or diminish the non-Hermitian-induced skin effect.

This paper investigates the feasibility of quaternary Golay complementary array pairs (GPCAPs) and demonstrates that such pairs exist only when the number of elements is even. Furthermore, we present a novel construction method for generating GPCAPs consisting of $2m$ elements.

This study presents the most stringent limits to date on anomalous Higgs boson vector boson couplings derived from the LHC's 13 TeV proton-proton collision data, utilizing a dataset with an integrated luminosity of 35.9 fb$^{-1}$. The analysis examines the Higgs boson production and decay processes involving on-shell WW and ZZ pairs, specifically focusing on channels where the vector bosons decay into four leptons. Results indicate that these constraints are sufficiently tight to exclude the existence of anomalous Higgs boson vector boson couplings at a level consistent with standard model predictions.

Although deep learning has significantly advanced the field of change detection, most current methods rely on supervised training, necessitating extensive labeled datasets that are often unavailable in real-world scenarios. In response, we introduce an unsupervised change detection approach utilizing only aligned image pairs. Our method employs a dual-encoder architecture to extract features from both inputs, followed by a dual-decoder structure designed to generate both shared and distinct representations. The shared representations facilitate image reconstruction, while the distinct representations are used to identify changes. Evaluated across three datasets—including two synthetic and one real-world benchmark—our results demonstrate that this unsupervised framework achieves performance comparable to leading supervised methods.

We refine the asymptotic estimate for $r_2(\mathbb{N})$, representing the cardinality of the set of squares summing to a natural number $n$, by improving upon prior bounds. Furthermore, we establish an asymptotic formula for the size of the additive complement of the set of squares, denoted as $A^c$, provided that $A$ possesses a positive upper Banach density. These findings extend and generalize previous work by various researchers, including the contributions of the authors themselves.

The Heisenberg spin exchange interaction is essential for silicon-based quantum technologies, yet its tunability remains limited. This study demonstrates that the interaction strength between phosphorus dopants in silicon can be precisely adjusted by controlling their placement along the <110> direction within the lattice. Utilizing a combination of first-principles calculations and effective Hamiltonian modeling, we show that introducing a single sulfur atom between two phosphorus atoms can diminish the exchange coupling by four orders of magnitude. These findings provide a new strategy for engineering exchange interactions, opening pathways to advanced silicon quantum architectures.

This paper addresses the transitivity degree for the group of birational auto-morphisms acting on certain rational varieties defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. Specifically, we determine the exact transitivity degree for the action of the birational automorphism group on smooth toric complete varieties. Additionally, we establish a lower bound for the transitivity degree concerning the birational self-equivalence groups of smooth Fano 3-folds.

This study examines the quantum mechanics of $N$-particle systems within non-abelian gauge theories, specifically deriving the corresponding Hamiltonian. We demonstrate that the system's collective momentum is the vector sum of individual particle momenta, while the total spin is likewise the sum of individual spins. Furthermore, we establish that the center-of-mass motion separates cleanly from relative particle motions. The paper also provides an explicit expression for the relative-motion Hamiltonian, which incorporates both Coulomb-like interactions and momentum-dependent terms.

We present a model for carrier generation within a semiconductor material that incorporates two-photon absorption. This framework utilizes a rate equation to describe the dynamics of the system, accounting for both one- and two-photon absorption processes. By applying a Fourier transform to this rate equation, we derive an analytical solution. Furthermore, we examine the conditions under which this solution remains valid and compare our theoretical predictions with results from numerical simulations.

We introduce a new dataset comprising 10,000 manually annotated examples of English misogynistic texts, which we utilize to train the MARBERT model. This model, a refined version of the Misogyny Awareness RoBERTa, demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in identifying misogyny within social media content. Furthermore, we evaluate several pre-trained language models and fine-tuned variants across multiple dimensions, including their ability to detect misogyny, their sensitivity to gendered language, and their generalization to unseen examples.

This paper investigates the existence and uniqueness of solutions to backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) incorporating a Markovian generator that depends on the solution's history. By leveraging a novel estimate for the specified type of BSDE, the authors establish both the existence and uniqueness of its solution.

Recent research has demonstrated that adding regularization to dynamics models can enhance the robustness of the resulting control policies. This study investigates how imposing a minimum threshold on likelihood noise within the model's dynamics influences this robustness. We establish a lower bound for the robustness of the learned controller and prove that the robustness increases as the likelihood noise approaches this bound. Furthermore, we introduce a regularization method that enforces a lower bound on likelihood noise, which improves control performance. Experimental results on both simulated environments and a physical robotic arm confirm these findings.

This study introduces a novel framework for coded caching by linking subfile assignments to combinatorial structures known as set systems. Leveraging this approach, the paper establishes upper and lower bounds on achievable performance for various strategies. Specifically, it demonstrates that the optimal Lattice Index Coding (LIC) strategy yields an optimal linear coded caching scheme when applied to linear methods. Furthermore, the work extends the framework to address non-linear schemes by presenting a general method for deriving performance bounds.

This work introduces a predicative and constructive formulation of the Scott model, originally developed in [10], which serves as a semantic foundation for Martin-L\"of Type Theory augmented with proof irrelevance. We demonstrate that this model supports both the levelled syntax and the levelling-free variant of impredicative Martin-L\"of Type Theory. Furthermore, we establish the consistency of this semantic framework by proving the key results of semantic soundness and completeness.

This paper investigates degenerate Eisenstein series associated with Weyl group cosets and establishes their modular properties through an application of our prior work on twisted partition functions.

Collision avoidance is a critical area of research within robotics. This study introduces a novel method for detecting collisions in mobile robotic arms by integrating the spatial configuration of the system into the traditional velocity obstacle framework. By employing the concept of velocity obstacles, the approach generates a collision-free trajectory for the robot's motion. The incorporation of spatial configuration into this framework results in a non-convex constraint, which the study addresses by utilizing a Riemannian optimization technique. The validity of the proposed method is demonstrated through simulations involving a mobile robotic arm navigating an environment with static obstacles.

Natural language processing (NLP) aims to address challenges posed by the diversity in written and spoken forms, a goal that has been significantly advanced by deep learning. This paper introduces a deep learning framework designed to generate concise summaries of long documents, utilizing a novel attention mechanism that enables the model to selectively focus on critical sections of the input text.

We introduce a method for implementing nonlinear Hadamad gates within Bose-Einstein condensates, enabling the enhancement of Ramsey interferometry through the generation of a spin-squeezed state. This approach employs a single-photon detector to measure the condensate's population, triggering a feedback loop that drives the system toward the squeezed dark state. We demonstrate that this technique surpasses the standard quantum limit, achieving a performance gain of up to 10 dB.

This paper investigates the intersection properties of meromorphic maps within the context of $n$-dimensional complex projective spaces ($\mathbb{C}P^n$) and $m$-dimensional complex projective spaces ($\mathbb{C}P^m$). Specifically, it examines scenarios where a map interacts with a collection of $n+1$ generic hypersurfaces or $m+1$ generic hyperplanes. Furthermore, the study analyzes the behavior of non-degenerate maps under the influence of a single hypersurface alongside $m$ generic hyperplanes.

This paper introduces novel signature-based Gröbner basis algorithms designed to leverage the specific properties of polynomial systems arising from ideals of intersection. These methods improve computational efficiency by integrating the SPU (Signature Preserving Unitrization) algorithm with the FG (Faugère's $F_4$) framework. Experimental results demonstrate that these proposed methods significantly outperform the standard $F_4$ algorithm when applied to specific classes of intersection polynomial systems.

This study examines the photon rapidity density in Cu+Cu collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$ GeV, utilizing experimental data from the PHENIX detector. The analysis employs Glauber model calculations to estimate the Cu+Cu cross section and compares these findings with Au+Au collisions at the same energy level. The results indicate that the photon rapidity density in Cu+Cu collisions is approximately 10% of that observed in Au+Au collisions. Additionally, the rapidity density of charged particles in Cu+Cu collisions is roughly 70% of the value seen in Au+Au collisions. Consequently, the photon-to-charge particle ratio in Cu+Cu collisions is comparable to that in p+p collisions at the same energy.
