This paper examines smooth quadrics within the framework of projective spaces over arbitrary fields.

TextWorlds serve as an open-source framework for natural language-driven virtual environments, primarily utilized for benchmarking and assessing AI agents capable of reasoning about texts. Recently, the community introduced TextWorldExpress, a specialized version optimized for Python that significantly boosts simulation throughput. However, this enhanced performance comes at the expense of interpretability, as the internal mechanics are obscured by complex dependencies. To address this gap, we present an alternative, high-speed implementation in Python that maintains full transparency. Named TextWorldExpress-Py, this version replicates the superior performance of its predecessor while ensuring the codebase remains understandable and modifiable.

We examine the influence of three-dimensional Topological Insulator (TI) edge dislocations on electronic transport. By employing a tight-binding model, we demonstrate that these dislocations host a one-dimensional conducting state localized at their core. Furthermore, we show that this state enables the propagation of electrons along the dislocation line, even in the presence of strong disorder.

This paper investigates the existence and uniqueness of $p$-harmonic functions within specific unbounded regions. Our findings demonstrate that for a particular class of domains, a unique positive $p$-harmonic function exists only when the parameter $p$ is sufficiently large. Conversely, if $p$ is small enough, an infinite family of such positive functions can be constructed.

This study investigates the spatial dependence of extreme events across the North Atlantic Ocean using Metop satellite data. The analysis reveals that, when conditioned on rare Metop wind speed events, spatial correlation for wind speed and wave height follows an exponential decay over distances exceeding 500 km. Furthermore, the paper introduces a novel Bayesian framework designed to estimate the parameters of this extremal spatial dependence. The proposed method is validated through a simulation study and applied to the North Atlantic dataset.
We establish that the hyperbolicity of a variety guarantees the non-existence of certain types of rational points, extending previous findings by our work.

The interpretation of manipulability matrices or ellipsoids as tangent spaces within Riemannian manifolds has been proposed in the literature. This paper offers a rigorous validation of that perspective by providing an alternative derivation of the manipulability ellipsoid, utilizing the concepts of Riemannian metrics and geodesics.

This study investigates the capability of the High-Luminosity LHC to detect the Standard Model Higgs boson through its decay into bottom quarks, specifically in association with top quark pair production ($t\bar{t}b\bar{b}$). The analysis focuses on the $t\bar{t}b\bar{b} \to \ell\nu b\bar{b}jj$ channel, where the top quarks decay leptonically and hadronically, respectively. By employing a multivariate analysis technique, the study demonstrates that the High-Luminosity LHC can achieve a $5\sigma$ discovery significance for a $125$ GeV Higgs boson with an integrated luminosity of $300$ fb$^{-1}$.

This study introduces a multi-phase training strategy designed to enhance canonical pose acquisition for 3D object estimation systems. We begin by training a coarse localization module to identify object instances within scenes. Subsequently, we train a refinement network to generate precise canonical poses specifically for the detected objects. Finally, we employ a distillation approach to integrate the outputs of both networks into a single unified model. Experimental results demonstrate that this method significantly surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in canonical pose learning.

We introduce a new framework designed to analyze public sentiment regarding vaccine misinformation and its evolution over time. This approach employs a multi-modal, multi-task deep learning model that integrates both textual and visual data to automatically identify the presence of misinformation and gauge associated attitudes. Additionally, we have created a novel attention mechanism to synthesize information from diverse modalities, enabling a more nuanced understanding of sentiment. Empirical results from our experiments demonstrate that this framework outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.

We introduce a novel strategy for controlling the central energy and temporal duration of attosecond pulses by manipulating the carrier-envelope phase (CEP) of the driving laser within a single-cycle regime. This approach generates high-harmonic spectra that are both narrow and broad, yielding isolated attosecond pulses at the extreme ultraviolet range. This work demonstrates that CEP manipulation offers a viable method for tailoring the characteristics of CEP-stable isolated attosecond pulses.

We have conducted a comprehensive analysis of Algol~C's orbital period using 120 years of photometric data from the TESS mission, spanning from 2018 to 2022. By applying a Lomb-Scargle periodogram to the TESS light curves, we identified a stable 2.896911-day cycle, which aligns with previous findings. Furthermore, a Bayesian Markov Chain Monte Carlo approach was utilized to refine the orbital ephemeris, yielding a period of $2.8969110 \pm 0.0000001$ days. This new result is consistent with prior studies and demonstrates a high degree of stability over the observed timeframe. Additionally, we investigated Algol~C's variability by analyzing the power spectral density of the TESS data, revealing a complex spectrum of frequencies. This complexity arises from the interplay of the primary orbital period and its numerous harmonics, alongside a distinct 1.5-day cycle.

This paper examines the blow-up behavior of positive solutions to the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation within a bounded domain subject to a Dirichlet boundary condition. We demonstrate that standard blow-up techniques applicable in the whole space can be extended to this bounded-domain scenario. Furthermore, we establish blow-up results under initial data satisfying conditions analogous to those of the critical mass and critical energy.

Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as a potent method for resolving partial differential equations (PDEs) by leveraging their adaptability to various PDE types and their capacity to integrate multiple data sources. However, PINNs often suffer from inefficient training, a challenge that becomes increasingly severe with higher-dimensional problems. This study introduces a novel strategy termed the Residual-based Adaptive Node Generation (RANG) approach, designed to enhance training speed. RANG dynamically adjusts the distribution of collocation points throughout the process by generating new nodes in regions where PDE residuals remain elevated. Empirical results across various benchmark problems demonstrate that RANG significantly accelerates training, particularly for high-dimensional scenarios. Furthermore, the study offers theoretical analysis supporting the claim that RANG accelerates PINN convergence.

This study introduces a new analytical framework for modeling the conduction band structure of periodic ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs). The proposed method is validated against finite element simulations and demonstrates superior performance in handling the nonlinearity and complexity inherent in solving the conduction band equation. Furthermore, the paper examines how domain periodicity influences the conduction band profile and evaluates the efficacy of various domain engineering strategies.

The Rust programming language community has recently established a centralized repository for its libraries known as Cargo, which has grown to host over 100,000 members. This study examines the security posture of this expanding ecosystem by analyzing 100,000 libraries and 300,000 unique dependencies, identifying 1,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,0

This study investigates the stochastic complex Ginzburg-Laudau equations driven by a pure jump noise. We demonstrate the existence of a unique strong solution and prove the convergence of an associated approximation scheme. Furthermore, we analyze the ergodic properties of the system, establishing both the strong Feller property and ergodicity. Finally, we derive an explicit rate of convergence toward the invariant measure under the influence of the pure jump noise.

This paper investigates the power graph of specific finite noncyclic abelian groups, deriving formulas for their minimum degree and providing conditions that determine whether the graph is connected, bipartite, or split.

This study examines the energy of the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) at the LHC's peak operating levels, utilizing data from the UA5 experiment. The analysis leverages the distribution of transverse momenta observed in proton-proton collisions with a center-of-mass energy of 300 GeV, alongside data from proton-nucleus interactions at the same energy. By applying the QCD framework for small Bjorken-$x$ and the color glass condensate model, the research investigates the energy dependence of the gluon density within nuclei.

This study introduces a novel framework for landmark detection and recognition that integrates local and global features. The approach utilizes Landmark Gabor Filters (LGFs) to generate robust local descriptors, while the global structure is captured through a landmark-based pose model. The system's efficacy is validated through experiments on the landmark-rich ICLP dataset, which features 100 distinct human poses, as well as the more complex, pose-diverse MPII dataset containing 100 different activities.

Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) are renowned for their ability to handle node features and structural data effectively. However, their reliance on gathering features from neighboring nodes introduces a computational bottleneck, as this process scales linearly with graph density. To address this, we propose a novel technique that shuffles the sequence of feature collection within GCNs. This approach not only accelerates computation but also enhances model performance. We validate the efficacy of our method through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

This study introduces a novel, highly adaptable image Trojan attack that surpasses existing methods in real-world applicability. Unlike previous attacks constrained by specific target models, our approach successfully transfers to various convolutional neural networks, including VGG, ResNet, and Inception. Furthermore, the proposed method eliminates the need for any fine-tuning or retraining of the target architecture. Experimental results demonstrate an attack success rate of 99.9% on VGG16, 99.8% on ResNet50, and 99.7% on VGG16. Additionally, the generated perturbations remain imperceptible to the human eye.

The ROSIE Integral Field Unit (IFU) is a novel instrument designed for the MMT, featuring a 1.2-metre solid-state camera capable of capturing 1024x1024 pixels. Its field of view spans 1.2 arcminutes, enabling high-resolution spatial mapping of diverse celestial targets, including planetary nebulae, star clusters, and galaxies. This capability allows for the creation of 3D data cubes with a spatial resolution of 0.04 arcseconds and a spectral resolution of 0.00004 arcseconds. This paper details the initial observations made using ROSIE, covering both near-infrared and optical wavelengths.

This study examines the low-energy $S$-factors for the $^3$He($^3$He,2p)$^4$He reaction, employing a model that accounts for Coulomb dispersion and the finite size of nuclei. The derived $S$-factors are compared against experimental data and previous theoretical models. Additionally, the research evaluates the impact of these low-energy $S$-factors on the nuclear fusion occurring within stars.

We introduce a novel method for determining the mineralogical composition and internal structure of potential exo-Earths orbiting Sun-like stars, utilizing the technique of asteroseismology. By analyzing the stellar oscillation frequencies, we can infer the mass and radius of these planets. We then apply a forward modeling approach to generate synthetic seismic data based on various planetary models, which are subsequently compared against the observed asteroseismic signals to constrain the planets' internal architecture and mineralogy. Our results indicate that for a significant number of target systems, the inferred properties of exo-Earths are comparable to Earth's. Furthermore, the methodology is capable of detecting deviations in planetary composition and structure, offering valuable insights into the formation and evolution of planetary systems.

This study introduces a novel deep learning framework for massive MIMO that leverages attention-based channel state information (CSI) to enhance feature extraction. By integrating attention mechanisms into convolutional neural networks (CNNs), the proposed method effectively suppresses unimportant features while highlighting significant ones. Furthermore, a specialized loss function is designed to enhance the model's resilience against noise-contaminated CSI. Simulation results demonstrate that the attention-driven approach outperforms standard CNNs in classification accuracy and exhibits superior stability when processing noisy channel data.
This work presents a unified framework for the semantics of modal logic based on topological categories, thereby extending and generalizing multiple existing topological approaches.

In 1990, Leeb and Stiebitz conjectured that every bipartite graph with a maximum degree of 3 admits a strong edge-coloring requiring no more than 10 colors. This paper refutes that conjecture by providing a counterexample constructed as a subgraph of the Cartesian product of two specific bipartite graphs, each possessing a degree of 3 and 4 vertices respectively.

This paper investigates the minimal support size for elements within the eigenspaces of $q$-Hamming graphs defined on $q$-tuples over an $n$-element set. We establish tight lower and upper bounds for this cardinality under various constraints regarding $n$, $i$, $j$, and $q$.

COPASI is a prominent, widely utilized application for computational systems biology. Although it offers a robust suite of analysis tools, its desktop-based interface restricts user interaction to local execution. In contrast, ShinyCOPASI introduces a web-based R interface that empowers users to configure COPASI models, execute simulations, and visualize results directly within a browser. This package facilitates the integration of COPASI capabilities into diverse workflows, including standalone scripts, educational modules, and broader web applications.

Neural networks have emerged as a powerful tool for addressing inverse and ill-posed problems, offering an alternative to conventional methods. This study investigates the efficacy of neural networks in solving the inverse Stefan problem, a task characterized by a moving boundary. We propose a novel network architecture designed to generate solutions that strictly adhere to the physical constraints of the problem. Furthermore, we demonstrate through numerical experiments that this method is both effective and efficient.

This paper investigates the conditions under which the algebra of class functions constitutes a maximal abelian self-adjoint algebra (MASA) for certain quantum groups, including $SU_q(2)$ and $O_q(4)$.

This study introduces a new inexact policy iteration method utilizing inexact GMRES to solve the linear systems within the algebraic loop of Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). We establish the convergence of this proposed inexact GMRES policy iteration under specific conditions regarding system residuals. Numerical experiments demonstrate that in a large-scale MDP comprising 10,000 states, the inexact GMRES approach achieves a 100-fold speedup over traditional policy iteration.

This paper investigates ordinary and symbolic powers within the framework of weighted oriented graphs. We establish that for such graphs, ordinary and symbolic powers are equal. Additionally, we provide an explicit formula for the degree of the elimination polynomial associated with the edge ideal of a graph.

Computer simulations are frequently employed to model physical systems, yet the associated parameter estimation through inverse problems often proves difficult due to prohibitive computational costs. This study introduces a novel methodology for refining computer simulator performance by leveraging an adaptive, data-driven metamodel. This approach offers two primary advantages: (i) it facilitates the resolution of inverse problems by enabling the utilization of noisy observational data, and (ii) it supports the execution of computationally intensive tasks such as global sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification. The methodology's efficacy is demonstrated through two illustrative cases.

This study investigates the feasibility of distribution-free robust learning, a framework where algorithms must maintain bounded excess robust generalization error across all distributions. We demonstrate that for any concept class with finite VC dimension, robust learning is achievable only when the query radius exceeds a specific lower bound. Furthermore, we establish tight bounds for various standard concept classes, including halfspaces, parity functions, and intersections of halfspaces.

We examine the production of jets accompanied by an isolated photon in proton-proton collisions, focusing on the impact of photon radiation within the jets on the underlying kinematics. By analyzing the parton shower, we demonstrate that the inclusion of the photon modifies the pre-shower initial conditions for the partons. Consequently, this necessitates an adjustment to the standard factorization scale, which is shown to be raised by a factor of two when the photon is present. These findings are validated through perturbative QCD calculations at next-to-leading order (NLO) and matched with parton shower simulations at NLO accuracy.

This study establishes apéry-style series summations featuring an alternating pattern, utilizing the framework of colored multiple zeta values at specified weight levels. We demonstrate that these alternating forms can be expressed as linear combinations of their non-alternating counterparts, revealing a significant finding: the evaluation of the alternating series demands multiple zeta values of approximately half the weight level compared to non-alternating equivalents.

We report the first direct measurements of both distance and space velocity for the brown dwarf LHS 2929, achieved through high-resolution spectroscopy and high-precision astrometry. The Gaia Collaboration's parallax data yielded a distance of 17.14 ± 0.11 parsecs, while radial velocity and proper motion were determined to be 10.6 ± 0.2 km/s and 11.3 ± 0.1 km/s, respectively. These figures establish a total space velocity of 15.7 ± 0.2 km/s. Furthermore, the study utilized high-resolution spectroscopy to detect the brown dwarf's rotation, measuring a projected rotational velocity of 11.0 ± 1.0 km/s, which corresponds to a rotation period of 3.0 ± 0.3 days.

This study examines particle production across diverse collision environments, ranging from proton-proton to lead-lead interactions at the LHC, utilizing the EPOS-LHC model. We analyze the system-size evolution of various particle ratios, observing a consistent trend where these ratios shift from small to large systems in a manner resembling the transition from pp to $^{208}\text{Pb}$-$^{208}\text{Pb}$ collisions. Furthermore, we investigate the system-size dependence of elliptic flow ($v_2$) for both protons and anti-protons, finding that protons exhibit greater $v_2$ than their antiparticle counterparts across all centralities. Additionally, we investigate the transverse momentum dependence of this proton/antiproton $v_2$ difference, noting that the effect diminishes at higher $p_T$ values. Finally, we evaluate the system-size evolution of the proton/antiproton ratio as a function of $p_T$ and compare our findings with experimental data.

Double Parton Distribution Functions (DPDFs) represent an extension of single-parton distributions that account for correlations between two partons within a proton. This study introduces a novel methodology for extracting DPDFs from proton-proton collision data, leveraging the correlation between the initial-state partons. We demonstrate that this approach can be applied to various processes, including double vector boson production, alongside specific results for $W$ production.

The Moon and Mars offer abundant sources of regolith that could support future industrial activities, such as extraterrestrial manufacturing and building. This study evaluates the mechanical and physical properties of simulated regolith from both celestial bodies to assess their viability for producing ceramic materials. Specifically, we examine the effects of varying particle size distributions and compaction pressures on the green-state density and strength of these samples. The findings indicate that Martian regolith yields higher green-state density and strength compared to lunar regolith. Furthermore, utilizing a bimodal particle size distribution enhances the mechanical performance of the green state for both lunar and Martian materials.

This study examines the impact of fibre surface slip conditions on the creation of liquid film drops. By employing a simplified model that accounts for both surface tension and viscous forces, we demonstrate that slip at the interface can lead to the formation of multiple drops. Furthermore, we derive an analytical formula for the spacing between these drops, which aligns well with our numerical simulations.

We introduce a novel method for evaluating star formation rate (SFR) accuracy using the Prospector Bayesian inference framework, leveraging $\beta$ luminosity as a proxy for the true SFR. This approach is applied to a sample of 1,000 galaxies from the Galaxy Zoo project, which have redshifts ranging from 0.005 to 0.15 and are selected to possess $i$-band magnitudes fainter than 19.0. The study demonstrates that the inferred SFR from $\beta$ luminosity aligns well with Prospector's SFR estimates, showing a mean bias of only 0.002 dex and a scatter of 0.25 dex. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that Prospector's SFR estimates exhibit a systematic bias of 0.06 dex toward lower values for galaxies with SFRs below 0.01 $M_{\odot}$/yr, a discrepancy that is notably more pronounced in low-mass systems.

We demonstrate that certain exceptional braided auto-equivalences of orbifolds correspond precisely to specific quadratic categories, thereby uncovering an unexpected connection between these two mathematical structures. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between the exceptional generators of such equivalences and the quadratic categories employed in constructing them.

This work examines the regularity of the Fisher-KPP equation solution, $u(x,t)$, which evolves from discontinuous initial data. We demonstrate that for any $s \in (0,1)$, the solution belongs to the space $C^{s,2s}_{x,t}$ within the space-time domain $\mathbb{R} \times (0,\infty)$. Furthermore, we establish the existence of a positive constant $\varepsilon$ such that $u \in C^{1,\varepsilon}_{x,t}$ on $\mathbb{R} \times (0,\infty)$. These findings are derived by analyzing the regularity of the semigroup $T(t)$ associated with the linear component of the equation and applying the method of moving planes.

This paper outlines our team's approach to the UbiComp 2021 Challenge, which involves identifying written text from time-series sensor data. Our methodology begins by pinpointing the specific time intervals corresponding to handwriting, followed by the classification of the text within those intervals. We then present the results of our experiments.

This study introduces a novel approach to modeling duration that diverges from traditional methods by not assuming a fixed distribution shape. Instead, it employs a flexible mixture model where each component represents a distinct distribution. The number of these components is not predetermined but is inferred directly from the data. By applying this method to model the duration of unemployment benefits, the authors demonstrate that the resulting model offers superior predictive performance compared to conventional alternatives.

We introduce a Bayesian framework for enhancing the efficiency of ecological occupancy models by integrating auxiliary data from non-invasive sampling. This approach explicitly models the correlation between auxiliary detection probabilities and occupancy status, thereby reducing the number of sampling occasions required. We illustrate the method's application through a case study on tiger (*Panthera tigris*) occupancy in India, incorporating camera trap data. Additionally, we provide R code implementing this methodology within the 'spOccupancy' package.

Driven by the need to assist general practitioners and dermatologists in delivering more accurate and timely diagnoses, the project introduces a novel skin lesion classification system. This system is designed to detect and diagnose eight prevalent types of skin cancer, including melanoma, and utilizes a hybrid methodology combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with a Bayesian classifier. The study employs a dataset of 12,000 images sourced from the ISIC Archive, which has been manually annotated by experts. The research evaluates various architectures, including AlexNet, VGG16, VGG19, ResNet50, and InceptionV3, alongside a proposed model integrating these networks with a Bayesian classifier. Results indicate that the hybrid approach surpasses standalone models, achieving an accuracy of 86.64%, a precision of 86.64%, a recall of 86.64%, and an F1-score of 86.64%.

Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) serve as vital cosmological tools, yet their peak luminosities exhibit variability that standard models fail to fully capture. This study introduces a Correlation Penalty Term (CPT) designed to enhance the representation of this variability by penalizing training processes that neglect correlations between parameters. We applied CPT-enhanced modeling to the Pantheon dataset, demonstrating that it more accurately reflects the variability structure of SNe Ia compared to conventional approaches. Furthermore, we utilized CPT modeling to investigate the Hubble tension, revealing that the tension persists even when accounting for the newly established variability structure.

We have conducted a high-resolution (0.15 arcsec) analysis of the 21-cm neutral hydrogen (HI) line in the nearby starburst galaxy NGC 253 using the Green Bank Telescope. Our findings reveal a highly extended HI disk with a diameter of 10.5 kpc, which is significantly larger than the galaxy's stellar diameter of 2.5 kpc. The outer regions of this disk exhibit a pronounced warp, characterized by a maximum amplitude of 0.5 kpc at a radius of 5.5 kpc. Additionally, the rotation curve remains nearly flat out to 5.5 kpc, implying a total dynamical mass of 1.1 x 10^10 solar masses. We also identified a substantial HI outflow, with a mass outflow rate of 0.34 solar masses per year, representing 14% of the star formation rate. This outflow is most intense in the galactic plane and diminishes toward the edges, with a scale height of 0.5 kpc. The outflow's kinematics are consistent with a driving force originating from the central starburst region. Furthermore, the observed HI column density in the outflow is comparable to that of the galactic plane, suggesting that the outflowing gas is highly ionized. The combination of a massive HI disk and a powerful outflow points to a complex interplay between star formation and gas dynamics

This study examines the entrainment of a particle-laden plume within a co-rotating stratified medium, utilizing both laboratory experiments and numerical simulations. The findings indicate that entrainment intensifies when plume buoyancy opposes particle-induced buoyancy, a phenomenon attributed to enhanced mixing resulting from opposing forces. The observed entrainment coefficients align well with predictions from the model proposed by Shao et al. (2019). Furthermore, the study analyzes the evolution of mean flow and turbulence characteristics, demonstrating that the impact of particles on turbulence remains negligible in the entrainment zone.

This study examines a random hypergraph model featuring an infection process where a node becomes infected upon exposure to an infected neighbor, with interaction rates potentially varying by node. We establish sufficient conditions for the existence of an epidemic and derive an upper bound on the infection rate's decay rate. Additionally, we demonstrate that the final size of the infection exhibits a phase transition as a function of the degree distribution.

We introduce a theoretical framework to examine how compressive strain influences the spin texture of a ferromagnetic bilayer. This model is designed to account for the anisotropic modification of exchange stiffness and the presence of magnetocrystalline anisotropy. The resulting spin configurations are analyzed by solving the Landau-Lifshitz equation. The study reveals that spin textures can undergo significant alterations under strain, specifically transforming from vortex states into vortex bubbles. The paper further outlines the conditions under which this transition occurs and provides a theoretical explanation for the observed phenomena.

This study investigates how rotation rate influences the frequency of magnetic cycles in weakly rotating stars through 3D global dynamo simulations. We analyzed a series of kinematic dynamo models, each featuring a differential rotation profile and a time-dependent torsional oscillation component. Our results indicate that while the torsional oscillation triggers a magnetic cycle in a rapidly rotating model, its absence leads to irregular, non-cyclical behavior in a slowly rotating model. Furthermore, we explored the impact of varying the amplitude of the torsional oscillation on the slowly rotating case. Our findings reveal that increasing the amplitude can induce a magnetic cycle, although the resulting cycle characteristics depend on the specific amplitude value. These outcomes suggest that kinematic dynamos in stars with slow rotation are capable of producing magnetic cycles when driven by torsional oscillations, a conclusion that supports the viability of the torsional oscillator-driven dynamo theory for solar-like stars.

We introduce a novel model designed to enhance performance in multi-input and multi-output learning scenarios. By employing a shared representation layer, the system learns a unified embedding that integrates data from various inputs, subsequently utilizing task-specific layers to generate predictions for each individual task. This architecture effectively addresses scenarios involving multiple inputs and outputs, including multi-task learning contexts. Empirical evaluations across six datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach surpasses current state-of-the-art methods.

This paper introduces McMini, a model checker designed for verifying multi-threaded programs that utilize locks and atomic instructions. Built upon the K framework, it employs an innovative, lightweight approach to thread scheduling that accelerates the exploration of state spaces. By utilizing a minimal scheduling strategy, McMini effectively concentrates its search on critical program states, resulting in significant performance gains. Empirical results demonstrate that it outperforms leading state-of-the-art checkers by factors of 10 to 100,000 when analyzing programs containing heavy lock contention.

Although WhatsApp has implemented initiatives to curb misinformation, the platform continues to serve as a primary conduit for spreading rumors. This study introduces a novel framework designed to identify rumor networks within WhatsApp groups by leveraging the distinct structural characteristics of these rumors. The authors developed a new algorithm for detecting rumor networks, which was benchmarked against existing methods using a dataset of 1,000 groups containing 1,000,000 messages. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches in rumor identification accuracy.

This study examines a population model featuring random mutations and selection, where each mutation alters an individual's type by a single step. We demonstrate that the population's type distribution evolves into a traveling wave, with the mutation rate determining the wave's speed. Additionally, we establish the existence of a stable, monotone, and time-periodic profile for this wave.

This study introduces a novel approach to detecting speech artifacts for spoofing countermeasures, leveraging attention mechanisms to automatically highlight relevant segments within audio signals. The proposed method is evaluated against the ASVspoof 2019 Logical Access (LA) task, demonstrating that it surpasses all baseline techniques and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

This work explores the relationship between supergravity, low-energy effective theories, and various frameworks of quantum gravity. We examine how supergravity serves as a foundational building block for these related areas and analyze the specific methods used to derive effective descriptions from quantum gravity models.

We introduce a novel method for reversing the pump propagation direction within a silicon microdisk, enabling the generation of correlated photon pairs traveling in opposite directions. This approach relies on a dual-waveguide configuration where a directional coupler facilitates the backscattering of a continuous-wave pump laser. By analyzing the second-order coherence functions, we demonstrate that the resulting spatially separated twin beams exhibit distinct statistical properties: the beam aligned with the microdisk's primary propagation mode displays strong bunching, whereas the counter-propagating beam shows no such statistical signature.

This study examines the electrical characteristics of buffer-oxide-etched (BOE) silicon nanowires (SiNWs) and contrasts them with those of standard etched SiNWs. Measurements of carrier concentration reveal that the BOE SiNWs possess significantly higher concentrations than their conventionally etched counterparts. Furthermore, the study analyzes the impact of varying annealing temperatures on these nanowires, demonstrating that elevated temperatures enhance carrier concentration and mobility within the standard etched SiNWs.

We demonstrate that partitioning the real line into cardinality $\aleph_1$ sets is possible under two distinct conditions: first, when the parts are Borel sets, and second, when the parts are closed sets. In contrast, we show that it is impossible to partition the real line into $\aleph_1$ sets if the parts are required to be open.

This study investigates the link between Commodity Trading Advisors (CTAs) and short-term reversal strategies. Our findings indicate a positive correlation between CTA activity and short-term reversal trading, suggesting a potentially symbiotic relationship where CTAs profit from these strategies while providing market liquidity. Furthermore, we observe that CTA positions in reversal trades are more pronounced during periods of elevated volatility and asset illiquidity.

Recent research has focused on developing detection systems for malicious traffic, including methods like Dynamic Protocol Detection (DPD) that utilize machine learning to identify anomalous protocols. Although these DPD approaches are effective, they remain vulnerable to evasion attacks. This paper introduces a new attack vector specifically designed to bypass DPD systems, demonstrating that even minor alterations to packet structures can cause significant failures in detection. To counter these threats, we propose a mitigation strategy that enhances detection robustness. Experimental results confirm both the severity of the proposed evasion attacks and the effectiveness of our suggested solution.

We investigate the interaction between magnons within an antiferromagnetic film and quasiparticles in an adjacent normal metal strip that exhibits the superconducting state. By employing the Green's function technique, we derive an effective Hamiltonian for the magnetic film, which accounts for the influence of the superconducting strip. Our analysis demonstrates that this configuration modifies the magnon dispersion relation, specifically inducing a frequency shift. Furthermore, we calculate the magnon density of states and examine how it is altered by the presence of the strip.

This study introduces a zero-shot framework designed to mitigate federated learning challenges arising from unseen data distributions. By employing a newly proposed meta-regularization alongside a zero-shot regularity assessment, the approach enables clients to generate high-quality synthetic samples tailored to their local non-i.i.d. characteristics. These generated distributions subsequently serve as effective regularizers for local model training. Extensive experiments across various zero-shot scenarios demonstrate that this method significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches.

We introduce an efficient, scalable method for executing the quantum Fourier transform (QFT) on high-dimensional multi-photon systems. This approach is designed to facilitate the advancement of future quantum computing and communication technologies operating at elevated dimensions.

This paper addresses channel estimation for IRS-assisted communication systems, focusing on the joint estimation of cascaded channel coefficients between the base station and IRS, as well as the IRS and user equipment. We propose a lightweight, optimization-based method that formulates the task as a constrained optimization problem, solved via successive convex approximation. This approach eliminates the need for pilot signals, thereby enhancing spectral efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed scheme outperforms existing pilot-based methods in terms of bit error rate performance while simultaneously reducing computational complexity.

This study examines the volume and content of local news regarding COVID-19 across 1,000 U.S. markets, utilizing data from NewsFacts.org. The research employs both descriptive statistics and econometric models to analyze these metrics. The findings indicate that the volume of COVID-19 coverage is driven by the virus's spread, the timing of state-level interventions, and the political leanings of local media outlets. Furthermore, the study finds that the content of the reporting is significantly shaped by the extent of the pandemic and the timing of government actions.

Recent studies have demonstrated that neural extrapolation is possible, suggesting that neural networks can learn to generalize beyond the scope of their initial training data. However, existing research primarily focuses on specific, often trivial, tasks. This paper investigates the extent to which neural networks can perform systematic extrapolation—a skill that involves counting and generalizing to novel domains. Our findings indicate that systematic extrapolation enables counting capabilities far exceeding those of traditional methods and training limits. Furthermore, we show that this ability transfers across different tasks and domains. Finally, we discuss the implications of these results for understanding human learning mechanisms.

Bloom filters are highly efficient, low-memory data structures used to test whether an element exists in a set. However, their standard implementation suffers from false positives, a drawback that xored filters address by significantly reducing memory usage while maintaining superior speed compared to Bloom filters. This paper introduces a novel variation called the xored filter with delayed decoding, which retains the minimal memory footprint and velocity of xored filters but eliminates false positives entirely.

This paper investigates the Alexandrov body construction within an algebraic geometric framework, revealing a connection to divisorial Zariski decomposition. We demonstrate that the convex Alexandrov body of a pseudo-effective divisor on a smooth projective variety corresponds precisely to the closure of the set of pseudo-effective divisorial Zariski decomposition. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between the faces of this convex body and specific minimal models associated with the underlying divisor.

We introduce a methodology to determine the appropriate time scale for capturing market directional information, grounded in the premise that the optimal granularity is dictated by historical transaction volumes. By applying this approach to both simulated and actual data, we demonstrate the technique's efficacy.

The clustering algorithm developed by F.L. Voogd is recognized as a privacy-preserving method because it processes data exclusively in a non-sensitive format, ensuring privacy by excluding raw sensitive details from the clustering workflow. This study introduces a novel implementation of the F.L. Voogd algorithm within a secure multi-party computation (SMC) framework, enabling the secure clustering of private data across multiple parties without revealing underlying sensitive information. The proposed SMC-based approach relies on fundamental SSMC protocols, specifically secure comparison, secure summation, and secure multiplication. The paper details the algorithm's design, analyzes its computational complexity, and demonstrates its practical viability through an implementation in the Secured Computation Library (SCAPE).

Sim2real transfer is a critical issue in machine learning, particularly within the context of autonomous vehicle competitions like the 2018 KITTI Autonomous Driving Challenge, where participants were required to train on simulated data and deploy on real hardware. This study investigates the extent to which models trained in simulation generalize to actual road conditions. Our findings indicate that while some transfer occurs, the degree of success varies significantly based on the specific task. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the efficacy of sim-to-real deployment is highly contingent upon the quality of the simulation environment.

The rapid advancement in deepfake technology has generated significant concern due to their heightened realism. This study introduces a novel approach to generating deepfakes by employing a conditional diffusion model that utilizes a single video clip as input. The methodology involves swapping the identity of the source video with that of a target subject, resulting in realistic outputs. The authors present a new dataset comprising 1,000 video pairs, each containing 10 seconds of footage at 25 frames per second and a resolution of 256x192, curated from YouTube. The proposed technique surpasses current state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative and qualitative assessments.

We introduce a new method for characterizing the atmospheres of temperate planets, which are those with equilibrium temperatures between 200 K and 1000 K. This approach relies on the distinct behaviors of carbon and nitrogen gases under varying atmospheric pressures. In massive atmospheres, the deep, hot layers drive carbon into carbon monoxide, whereas lighter atmospheres allow the upper, cooler regions to favor carbon dioxide. Conversely, the presence of abundant hydrogen enables nitrogen to exist as molecular nitrogen, while its absence results in the formation of dinitrogen. By analyzing the relative abundances of these species, we can determine whether a planet possesses a massive or light atmosphere. This technique is particularly effective for rocky worlds orbiting M-dwarf stars, where the resulting spectral signatures are most pronounced.

The Hopfield network, introduced in 1982, is a McCulloch-Pitts model capable of functioning as an associative memory. This study presents an enhanced learning algorithm for the McCulloch-Pitts network that surpasses the capabilities of the original Hopfield model. We demonstrate the efficacy of this proposed algorithm through various examples.

This paper introduces a new dataset comprising 100,000 OOV images dedicated to scene text recognition, designed to address challenges related to unseen characters. We also propose an OOV-specific regularization term for training, which functions as a constraint on the model's character distribution. Empirical results demonstrate that our proposed method surpasses existing approaches on the newly created OOV dataset and achieves state-of-the-art performance on the standard ICDAR 2015 test set.

We demonstrate how validated numerics can rigorously compute isolated branches of solutions for parameter-dependent systems exhibiting isolated solution branches, specifically using a Newton-Krylov method combined with pseudo-arclength continuation. This approach is applied to a model representing the Euler elastica subjected to point loads, where we rigorously trace solution paths across varying parameters and pinpoint bifurcation points with guaranteed accuracy.

This paper introduces a new approach to change point detection and failure mode isolation that leverages deep learning and the Bayesian framework. By utilizing a deep autoencoder to compress data into a compact representation, the method significantly lowers computational costs, thereby enhancing performance in resource-constrained settings. Furthermore, the study presents a novel technique for identifying failure modes based on the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of the posterior probability of

We have identified and analyzed the most massive, metal-rich accreted dwarf galaxies in the Milky Way using Gaia DR3 data, specifically targeting Gaia-Sausage Enceladus (GSE) and Wukong/LMS-1. By applying a novel method to isolate these systems, we detected approximately 1,000 GSE stars and roughly 1,000 Wukong stars, each exceeding 100 times the solar mass in mass. Our analysis reveals that both systems share nearly identical kinematic properties and exhibit a common abundance pattern characterized by elevated alpha-element ratios relative to iron. Notably, the GSE system displays a significantly steeper [Mg/Fe] versus [Fe/H] trend compared to Wukong, suggesting a difference in progenitor stellar mass distributions. Furthermore, the distinct [Mn/Fe] trends observed in both systems indicate that their respective progenitors had different initial mass functions. We model the chemical evolution of both systems as single-component dwarf galaxies, finding that Guk formation persisted for approximately 1.5 billion years in Guk and roughly 2 billion years in Wukuk. These findings imply that Guk and Wukuk were likely the most massive dwarf galaxies accreted by the Milky Way, with Wukuk being slightly more massive than Guk.

This work examines the homotopy orbit spectrum $(Z[[G]])_{hG}$ formed from the completion of the classifying spectrum of a profinite group $G$. It is demonstrated that under specific conditions, this object is equivalent to $Z$. Furthermore, the study provides an explicit description of the resulting spectrum when $G$ is a finitely generated profinite $p$-group.

In semi-supervised learning, the goal is to develop effective models using minimal labeled data alongside abundant unlabeled information. This paper introduces a novel approach to selective labeling that leverages uncertainty quantification to identify the most beneficial data points for annotation. Our method employs a deep pseudo-labeling framework enhanced with a novel mechanism for quantifying prediction uncertainty. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate that our selective labeling strategy significantly outperforms existing methods.

The EuS/InAs interface is renowned for its topological Kondo insulator properties, yet the electronic characteristics of the individual layers remain poorly understood. In this study, we utilize scanning tunneling spectroscopy to investigate the electronic structure of a single atomic layer of EuS deposited on InAs. Our findings reveal that dispersed states originating from the InAs valence band maximum extend into the EuS band gap, indicating strong interfacial coupling between InAs and the topological surface states of the grown layer. Furthermore, we observe a pronounced dependence of the InAs valence band's dispersion on the specific tunneling position, suggesting that the EuS layer modifies the InAs band structure through strain effects.

This paper demonstrates that Borel Wadge determinacy can be derived from second-order arithmetic augmented with the axiom of $\Pi^1_1$-induction along with transfinite induction up to the Kleene-Brouwer order defined on $\mathbb{N}^\mathbb{N}$.

Pruning is a primary technique for accelerating neural network inference, yet existing methods often fail to fully exploit the inherent parallelism of modern hardware. This paper introduces "ClickTrain," a novel pruning approach that maximizes parallelism by selectively removing entire layers based on their individual contribution to the network's output. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that ClickTrain achieves up to a 2.5x speedup over state-of-the-art pruning strategies. Furthermore, the method is versatile, successfully applying to various network architectures including ResNet, VGG, BERT, and GPT.
This paper introduces a relational semantic framework for substructural modal logics and demonstrates that these logical systems possess the strong property of completeness.

The detection of gravitational waves and electromagnetic radiation from the neutron star merger event GW170817 confirmed that such mergers produce multi-messenger signals. This paper explores the potential for future events to generate detectable radio and X-ray emissions alongside gravitational waves, specifically analyzing how the simultaneous observation of both can constrain the equation of state for neutron star matter. We demonstrate that combining these observations allows for tighter limits on the radius of a 1.4 solar mass neutron star, narrowing the range to 10.6--12.4 km at 90% confidence. Furthermore, we show that the inferred minimum tidal deformability is constrained to $\Lambda_{\rm min}=107$ at 90% confidence. These findings indicate that the synergy between gravitational wave and electromagnetic data offers significant advantages in refining our knowledge of the equation of state for dense nuclear matter.

TOI-5542b is a super-Neptune orbiting a K-dwarf star, identified as a valuable case study for investigating planetary composition and formation. This study presents the results of a multi-epoch, multi-wavelength photometric analysis of the system, which includes data from the TESS mission and ground-based observations conducted by the 1.5m, 1.8m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m, 2.1m,

This study introduces a sampling-based primal-dual algorithm designed to address stochastic convex decision-making problems involving both continuous and discrete variables. By leveraging the dual decomposition technique, the method iteratively refines both primal and dual policies to enhance operational strategies. Furthermore, a sampling-based approach is employed to estimate subgradients of the dual objective, ensuring convergence to optimal policies within a specific error margin. The paper also details a specific instantiation of this algorithm for the stochastic network design problem and validates its efficacy through numerical experiments.

This study introduces a deep learning framework designed to recognize 938 distinct mathematical symbols, including operators, delimiters, and letters. The system utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on a newly created dataset, with a k-nearest neighbors (kNN) classifier specifically engineered to enhance accuracy. The research evaluates various configurations of the kNN approach, ultimately achieving a peak recognition rate of 98.61%.

We demonstrate that the exponential growth of index degeneracies for BPS states on the Hilbert scheme of $k$ points over $\mathbb{C}^2$ is governed by an explicit formula. This formula involves the Euler characteristics of specific line bundles defined on the resolution of the singular locus within the Hilbert scheme.

This study investigates how the bridging characteristics of a network influence the predictability of epidemic diffusion. We introduce a novel metric, the bridging coefficient, designed to quantify the extent to which a specific node enhances network connectivity. Our findings indicate that while the bridging coefficient is highly effective at identifying pivotal nodes in the propagation process, the overall predictability of the outbreak is maximized in networks that are moderately bridged rather than those that are extremely so. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the optimal level of moderate bridging yields superior predictability compared to relying solely on nodes with high degrees or long lifespans.

This study introduces a novel approach to safety in reinforcement learning by employing a constraint-guided curriculum that prioritizes safety restrictions. By sequencing tasks from simple to complex based on their adherence to these limits, the method significantly lowers the frequency of safety breaches and accelerates the development of compliant policies. Furthermore, the authors demonstrate that this progressive framework enhances overall performance on challenging tasks by leveraging learned skills. Empirical evaluations across three distinct environments confirm the approach's efficacy.

This paper introduces a novel method for identifying twin primes through their prime generators, establishing a new prime-based numbering system. We derive a general formula for these prime generators and establish several theorems regarding the properties of twin primes. Additionally, we present two additional findings: a closed-form expression for the $n$-th prime number and a new criterion for determining the primality of odd integers.

This study introduces a hierarchical control framework designed for mobile systems that rely on sonar data to navigate unstructured environments. The system's upper layer determines the path by integrating a probabilistic road map with a cost function derived from pre-processed sonar information. The lower layer executes this path by generating specific velocity commands for the vehicle. The proposed method was validated through simulations involving a wheeled robot moving across cluttered landscapes.

We present the results of a JWST NIRCam and NIRSpec observation of Nereid, Neptune's distant and irregular satellite, aimed at characterizing its surface composition and constraining its thermal properties. Our findings reveal a reddish surface with spectral features consistent with water ice, nitrogen ice, and tholins, closely resembling other large, icy bodies in the outer solar system. Thermo-physical modeling indicates a surface temperature of 39.5 ± 1.5 K, suggesting a thermal conductivity of 0.11 ± 0.04 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. These results imply a subsurface structure that is relatively heterogeneous, lacking the homogeneous composition seen in the moons of Jupiter and Saturn. Additionally, we offer preliminary constraints on Nereid's elemental makeup, estimating a bulk composition of 60% H₂O, 30% N₂, and 10% CH₄ by mass.

This paper investigates the extension of affine planes derived from the projective line of a ring $R$ to form projective planes. We establish that such extensions exist precisely when $R$ is a local ring. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for projective lines over local rings, any two resulting projective planes are isomorphic to one another.

We demonstrate that employing the Tukey-order on countable models of arithmetic offers a straightforward method for establishing implications among various cardinal characteristics. This approach is utilized to provide concise proofs for numerous results originally developed by Brendle, Doucha, and Fuchs.

This study introduces an enhanced method for optimizing dynamic treatment strategies by merging the anti-optimism principle with Thompson sampling. We establish that this new approach achieves near-optimal performance, demonstrating an improvement of only a logarithmic factor compared to the best possible policy. Furthermore, we prove that incorporating gloominess into the sampling process is essential for attaining optimal outcomes.

This paper investigates the connection between resolving subcategories of finitely generated modules and the stability of higher algebraic K-theory groups under certain quotient categories. We establish that if a resolving subcategory $\mathcal{C}$ of finitely generated modules over a Noetherian ring $R$ possesses finite global dimension, then the higher K-groups of the quotient $\operatorname{K}_n(\operatorname{proj} R/\mathcal{C})$ remain invariant. Additionally, we demonstrate that for any two such resolving subcategories $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}$ with finite global dimensions, their intersection $\mathcal{C}\cap\mathcal{D}$ also maintains a finite global dimension.

We introduce a generalized framework for describing quantum states that encompasses both state preparations and measurement outcomes, thereby unifying the discussions of nonlocality and contextuality. Within this formalism, distinct state configurations can be interrelated through local transformations, which serve as the foundation for defining equivalence classes of states. We demonstrate that these equivalence classes are characterized by their respective sets of achievable correlations, and we further explore the relationship between state equivalence and the preservation of full rank properties under local transformations.

We introduce a novel many-body wavefunction featuring exact $\eta$-pairing ground states for multi-band Hubbard frameworks. This study examines the $\eta$-pairing order parameter, energy gaps, and correlation functions across varying inter-band hopping strengths and interaction parameters. Our findings indicate that the most robust pairing emerges at half-filling, with the order of magnitude of the gap governed by the competition between intra- and inter-band interactions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that correlations exhibit significant non-locality, a trait that intensifies as the disparity between interaction strengths grows.

This paper investigates the $a$-adic solenoid version of G.P\'olya's theorem, which includes a related generalization. We demonstrate that the associated analogous Polya formula admits solutions as continuous functions within the $a$-adic solenoid framework. Furthermore, we establish the solvability of the corresponding functional equation within the $a$-adic solenoid context.

Clustering presence-absence data is a prevalent analytical technique across numerous disciplines. This study evaluates various clustering approaches, including those based on dissimilarity, mixture models, and trees, and compares their performance against one another.

This study introduces a unified framework for detecting salient objects in RGB and RGB-d images, designed to leverage the complementary strengths of both data types. The proposed architecture employs a bidirectional mechanism to integrate information from multi-modal inputs, enhancing detection accuracy. Furthermore, a novel bidirectional attention module is developed to maximize the efficiency of processing these images. Experimental results demonstrate that this method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques in performance.

This study introduces a novel deep learning framework designed to identify abusive language in tweets, leveraging both text and image data. By integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs), the system effectively captures the spatial features of emojis and the sequential structure of words. Evaluated against the Emojify dataset, the model achieved a macro F1 score of 0.8921, demonstrating strong performance in detecting abusive content.

This paper investigates the count of integers that defy representation as palindromes in any base $b \ge 2$. We demonstrate that the proportion of such nonrepresentable integers approaches a limit of approximately $0.0848$, which is notably lower than the $0.0734$ threshold previously established for square numbers. Furthermore, we derive an asymptotic formula for the cumulative count of these nonrepresentable integers up to $x$, denoted as $U(x)$, which is $U(x) \sim C \frac{x}{\log \log x}$ with a constant $C \approx 0.0848$.

This study introduces a novel image reconstruction framework designed to address challenges arising from noise and inconsistencies within CT data. By integrating a unified model, we simultaneously tackle issues related to mixed noise and data inconsistency. The core of this approach involves a new mixed noise model that effectively captures noise characteristics across different levels, alongside a sparsity model tailored for data inconsistency. Furthermore, the framework employs a non-convex optimization formulation to enhance image reconstruction quality. To solve this non-convex problem, we developed an alternating minimization algorithm that decomposes the task into two subproblems: one solvable via the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) and another using the Conjugate Gradient method. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of reconstruction quality.

This paper introduces a novel approach to Bayesian Program Learning (BPL) designed to create minimal-data models capable of generating human-like handwriting. By employing a discrete latent variable representing the stroke order, the method constructs a generative model that simulates handwriting as a sequence of strokes. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this model in synthesizing character sequences from limited examples and show that its probabilistic framework enables the extraction of interpretable insights into the synthesized characters' formation processes.

This study introduces a novel storage scheme for generating three-nucleon interaction matrix elements within the j shell model. By leveraging the symmetries of the nucleon-nucleon interaction, the approach significantly reduces the necessary memory capacity. Furthermore, it outlines an optimized algorithm for efficiently calculating three-nucleon interaction matrix elements.

This paper examines various entanglement methodologies within quantum electronics, highlighting how each offers unique advantages. We analyze the correlator method, the von-Neumann density-matrix approach, and the characteristic function technique, demonstrating that the correlator method is particularly well-suited for investigating quantum electronic systems. Furthermore, we illustrate the practical utility of these entanglement concepts by applying them to two specific scenarios: a single-electron transistor and a quantum dot.
